Though his uncle assured us that he will bring the boy back, he didn't turn up." Sehgal said. He alleged that it was pre-planned as the parents of the students were aware of it. Paramjit's mother has assured us that he will come back before his visa expires.

In Kunal's case, they they came to know that one of his parents lived in the US. "When we came to know of his plans we kept a close vigil on him and even changed our place of stay. But he still managed to escape through the fire exit."

This act of the students has tarnished the school's image, he said, adding that the US authorities will take action against the students after their visa expires.

Hoshiarpur SSP Dr Sukhchain Gill said he has asked the DSP to probe the matter following a letter from the school authorities to the Jalandhar and Hoshiarpur SSPs. Jalandhar SSP Pawan Rai said: "We will see what action we can take legally in this matter."

It may be noted that last month over two dozen Catholic youth from Jalandhar had disappeared in New Zealand . Hoshiarpur and Jalandhar districts of Punjab are known for their expatriate community and people long to settle abroad through legal or illegal means.

Heading: Charkhi Dadri crash: family loses fight for more relief - Indian Express
Content:
A petition seeking a probe into the role of Fiona Mackeown, mother of slain British teenager Scarlett Keeling, in leaving her daughter in the company of a stranger will come up for hearing on Monday. Goa's Children's Court will hear the petition filed against Fiona by a local NGO, Utt Goenkara.

The NGO has asked that the CBI or any other competent agency should be directed to investigate the role of Fiona in leaving her 15-year-old daughter in the company of a stranger. Scarlett had come to India with her mother and was left with a boy named Julio. She was found dead on Goa's Anjuna beach on February 18 following which two persons were arrested and charged for drugging, raping and leaving her to die on the beach. The CBI is already investigating the murder case and the police have filed a chargesheet with the Children's Court here in this matter. Goa's Children's Court President Desmond D'Costa had issued notice to the state police and the state Government.

Aires Rodrigues, the NGO's representative, has alleged that Fiona was aware that her daughter was a minor and the law mandates that all children in Goa be provided safe environment wherein the parents are responsible for the child's safety.

Heading: Post-blasts, Rlys to introduce Integrated Security System - Indian Express
Content:
Over a decade after the Charkhi Dadri mid-air crash, the family of one of the victims of the "deadliest air collision" in history has lost its appeal for compensation from the Saudi Arabian Airlines.

The family lost the legal battle due to a single technicality of law that Saudi Arabian Airlines Corporation is a public body "wholly owned by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia". In short, the airline is out of bounds for Indian courts without prior sanction from the Centre, as the family of Farah Mumtaz, one of the passengers on board the Saudi Arabian Airlines flight on that fateful night, learnt on Friday. In fact, Section 86 (suits against foreign rulers, ambassadors and envoys) of the Civil Procedure Code states: "No foreign state may be sued in any court except with the consent of the Central Government certified in writing by a Secretary to that Government."

In a legal battle which started in 1998, the Mumtaz family claimed enhanced damages of "2,60,000 Francs equivalent to 17,030 grams of gold", as valued at the time of the judgment. As per the High Court, the Airlines had already paid Mumtaz's heirs over Rs 7.40 lakh.

The appeal before the Division Bench came after a Single Judge of the Delhi High Court in July 2001 found the relatives' plea "not maintainable" as they had failed to take prior permission from the Government to sue the Airlines.

Perusing the evidence on record, a Bench comprising Justices A K Sikri and J R Midha found that though the Airline Corporation is a "public and independent organisation", it was still "attached" to the Saudi Ministry of Defence and Aviation.

Confirming that the High Court had no jurisdiction to entertain the appeal, the Bench in its verdict observed on Friday: "It appears from the pleadings and documents that Constitution of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia indicates that it is a sovereign Islamic State — All the wealth under the ground or on the surface or in international territorial waters in the land or maritime domain is the property of the State."

The court refused to give credence to the family's argument that they had received Government sanction against the Corporation in November 2001, saying that the Single Judge had already passed his order in the month of July the same year.

Mid-air tragedy

On November 12, 1996 a Saudi Arabian Airlines flight from New Delhi to Dhahran in Saudi Arabia collided mid-air with an Air Kazakhstan aircraft over Charkhi Dadri in Haryana. All 349 people on board both flights were killed in the accident.

Heading: Rains sweep truck, 25 feared dead - Indian Express
Content:
The recent spate of bomb blasts in Bangalore and Ahmedabad has, somewhat ironically, expedited what years of arguments from the Railways Protection Force (RPF) could not.

Having sat over it for months, the Railways Ministry has given an "in-principle" nod to RPF's proposal to evolve an Integrated Security System at sensitive railway stations across the country, at a recently held meeting, say top ministry officials. The ministry has further agreed to buy necessary security equipment wherever necessary. "Formal instructions to this effect are likely to issued shortly," a senior railway official told The Indian Express.

Under the plan, the ministry is likely to outsource the installation, operation and maintenance of security-related equipment like vehicle scanners, CCTVs, X-Ray baggage screeners, door frame metal detectors (DFMDs) and explosive detectors to private players in lieu of granting them advertising rights for a fixed tenure. For some railway stations, the ministry plans to sanction outright purchase of these equipment. Estimates suggest that installing these systems would cost the Railways Rs 5 crore per station. About 150 stations will be covered to begin with.

The RPF, officials said, have already zeroed in on the best technologies available worldwide to implement this plan. "For instance, we plan to have CCTVs equipped with software which allow recording and storing of images. Similarly, we are proposing high-end vehicle scanners to scan the vehicle floors as soon as they enter the main gate of a station," an official said, adding that operation and maintenance of the equipment would have to be guaranteed by the providers.

Despite RPF batting strongly to implement this proposal for months now, the Railway Board, on some pretext or the other, has failed to take a decision on the matter in the past. But this time round, what helped the ministry decide in favour of the proposal is the response the RPF got to an Expression of Interest (EOI) it recently floated seeking private players to execute the Integrated Security Systems at major stations.

"As many as 43 players responded to our EOI. The who's who in the business, including players like Tata, BEL, ECIL, Wipro and HCL, have evinced interest in the proposal," a top railway official said. "All players have made detailed presentations over the past few weeks and we have been able to identify the best available technology worldwide which can work well in Indian conditions," he added.

Heading: Desperate search for missing chopper in Naxal territory - Indian Express
Content:
At least 25 people are feared dead after a lorry carrying them was swept away by strong currents on a flooded bridge in Guntur district.

The incident occurred around 12 noon when about 40 villagers were fleeing the flooded Narkulapadu village. Police said while seven bodies have been recovered, only eight persons could swim to safety. Guntur police control room said rescue teams located the truck in eight to 10 feet deep water. Police said they were trying to send fire personnel to try and extricate any bodies.

Police said the villagers had hired the truck as the AP state transport corporation had suspended services in the region.

Most of the rivers and rivulets were overflowing as heavy rains battered coastal and central Andhra on Sunday too. The Met Department has warned of more heavy rains across the state, especially in coastal Andhra in the next 24 hours.

The state Government has put the official death toll at 40 on Sunday.

Widespread rains continued in Warangal, Khammam, Nizamabad, Medak and Ranga Reddy districts. Krishna district received 10 cms rain in the last 24 hours. Hyderabad, which received 13 cms rain on Friday, received 9 cms rain on Saturday. Disaster Management Commissioner Ratna Prabha said 37,500 people living in low-lying areas have been shifted to 119 relief camps opened in Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy, West Godavari, Nalgonda, East Godavari, Krishna and Guntur districts.

Heading: Nayagarh attack: two Naxals in police net - Indian Express
Content:
Security personnel have now sought the help of locals to locate a private helicopter, with four crew members, which went missing over dense forests in the Maoist hotbed of Dantewara last week.

Naxalites had twice opened fire on the security forces searching the forests for the Ranbaxy-owned Ran Air helicopter Bell-430, which went missing an hour after taking off from Hyderabad last Sunday. Chief pilot V P Singh, co-pilot R Gaur, flight engineer Santosh Kumar and technician Ashwini Kumar were in the chopper when it went missing.

Bastar Divisional Commissioner Ganesh Shankar Mishra said revenue and forest staff in Dantewara have been asked to request the villagers to join the search as the Naxalites don't usually attack the locals. Pamphlets are being distributed in the district and its bordering areas in Andhra Pradesh, requesting people to join the search. A reward of Rs 1 lakh has been announced for anyone helping locate the missing chopper.

"It's a tough task for the security forces to venture deep into the forests, particularly in the hilly areas, as the Maoist guerillas attack from hilltops," a senior police officer told The Indian Express, adding that the search has to be carried out in the so-called Maoist "liberated zone" of South Bastar. Separate teams, comprising 150 security personnel each, have been engaged in operations to trace the helicopter, he added.

Four helicopters, including two of the Indian Air Force, had carried out an aerial search of the area after the crash. Images of the area taken by the National Remote Sensing Agency (NRSA), too, failed to yield any results. The ground searches were meanwhile affected by heavy rains with all rivers and rivulets, including Indravati in Bastar and Godavari of neighbouring Andhra Pradesh, in spate. Most roads and telephones lines in South Bastar are also cut off.

Meanwhile, relatives of the chopper crew have called on Chief Minister Raman Singh and demanded deployment of more security forces for the search operation.

Heading: Landslide snaps Goa-Karnataka link - Indian Express
Content:
Six months after the audacious attack by Maoists on establishments of the Orissa Police in Nayagarh district, the cops have arrested two extremists who played a key role in the February attack.

Though the two Maoists, Ranjan Rout and Prasanna Pal, were arrested on Friday night, the police revealed their identities only last night. The police claimed Pal is a member of the Central Core Committee of the Maoists organisation, and Ranjan a deputy commander. Jagatsinghpur SP R K Sharma said both played a key role in the Nayagarh attack. In fact, Prasanna was one of the 12-core committee members formed by Maoists for the Nayagarh attack, Sharma said.

Interrogations of the two have brought to light some Maoists strategies, their future plan of action and also on how the operations at Nayagarh were carried out. Police said the Nayagarh attack was planned in Gaya a year before. Police seized a few incriminating documents and a map from their possession. Both the rebels belong to Jagatsinghpur district.

Police officials said the Maoists are now trying to make inroads in Jagatsinghpur, where Posco is setting up its 12 million tonne steel plant.

On the night of February 15, 14 police personnel and a civilian were killed and four policemen wounded when around 500 heavily armed CPI-Maoist cadres attacked the Police Training School (PTS), the district armoury and district police station in coordinated attacks near Daspalla in Nayagarh district.

Heading: Four dead in Orissa - Indian Express
Content:
Heavy rains snapped Goa's southern link with neighbouring Karnataka following a major landslide along Anmod Ghat, a road running across Molem national wildlife sanctuary.

A hill along the highway, 5 km from Goa border in the ghat region, caved in causing the landslide in this narrow stretch traversing through thick forest. Long queue of vehicles transporting goods between both the states were stranded. Goa state administration has pressed into service its machinery to clear the debris. "We were not able to move the manpower and machinery at the spot as initially there was a traffic jam. It took hours for us to begin our work," a district administration official supervising the operations at the site said. Incessant rains have made the relief work more difficult, police said.

While the ghat landslide was being cleared, another landslide on the railway track few km away, was reported which disrupted south western railway trains. The landslide took place just next to Dudhsagar waterfall, a tourist spot tucked on the Western Ghat. Train services on south western railway remained disrupted till morning while the trains on Konkan railway route were moving at slower pace. "We already have our monsoons timetable in place and as per that the trains are running. We are apprehensive as the Konkan region is flooded," a KRCL official said.

Heading: Lightning kills 4 of family - Indian Express
Content:
Fears of fresh floods loomed over Orissa on Sunday as heavy rains triggered by a low pressure area pounded many parts of the state, raising water levels in major rivers and inundating low-lying areas. Four persons have been killed since Friday, official sources said here.

Normal life was affected by the incessant rains, snapping road links in several places, they said. Water level in several rivers, including Budha Balanga, Subarnarekha, Jalaka Britarani, Tel and Hati continued to rise, while that of Mahanadi, Brahmani, Rushikulya and Bansadhara were still below the danger mark, they said.

Release of water into the Hati river from Indravati dam has been stopped, while water level in rivers like Bansadhara fell as rains in Rayagada and neighbouring districts had stopped. Met office predicted heavy rainfall at isolated places over interior Orissa during the next 48 hours.

Heading: India plans to use upgraded vaccine to combat polio - Indian Express
Content: Four members of a family were killed and two others sustained burns when lightning struck them in Bihar's Rohtas district on Sunday. The incident occurred when the persons, working on a field, rushed to a nearby hut for cover from the incessant rain.

Heading: 22 MLAs meet Rajnath, want Khanduri out - Indian Express
Content:
With the efficacy of polio vaccine being increasingly questioned, India is contemplating using "high titre vaccine" to combat the virus.

Compared to the vaccine administered at present in the country, the high titre vaccine, which is also oral, carries more polio virus and considered more effective.

In an operation group meeting organised by the Union Ministry of Health on Saturday, experts from Enterovirus Research Centre in Mumbai disclosed that a pilot study using the 'new' vaccine has been conducted in Hyderabad and Indore. Samples of the study have been sent to the World Health Organisation (WHO), Geneva, for clearance. "It was a double-blind study. The vaccine was administered randomly and the trial management was carried out by WHO itself," Dr J M Deshpande, Director, ERC, told The Indian Express.

Experts in the Ministry said if WHO gives the go-ahead, high titre vaccine would replace the age-old vaccine all over the country. The vaccine would be first used in the high-risk areas of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar to eliminate P1 virus.

The Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare had recently disclosed in Parliament that out of the total 203 cases of polio reported in the country till April, 201 were administered polio vaccine.

Besides, the India Experts Advisory Group had asked the Government to explore the possibility of Injectable Polio vaccine or OPV. The suggestion was rejected as "it had been difficult to convince people to use oral vaccine. And if the vaccine was changed to injectable, they had to be convinced all over again. Also, the efficacy of oral and injectable vaccines did not show any considerable difference," said an official.

Heading: Cong threatens to launch stir over ‘lawlessness’ - Indian Express
Content:
The B C Khanduri Government in Uttarakhand is facing dissidence. A team of 22 legislators led by former chief minister Bhagat Singh Koshiari, and including some of the state ministers, reportedly met BJP president Rajnath Singh in Delhi on Sunday afternoon and sought Khanduri's replacement as the Chief Minister of the hill state.

This is the first time that the rebels in the ruling party have come out in the open with their demand. They claim that proper treatment is not being meted out to them as public representatives and it is the bureaucrats who are calling the shots. It is learnt that they have particularly pointed out the name of Khanduri's secretary Prabhat Kumar Sarangi.

The dissident leaders are also expected to meet senior leader and BJP's prime ministerial candidate Lal Krishna Advani later in the day. A senior party functionary, Anil Jain, is learnt to have met him already.

Meanwhile, Khanduri, who is also camping in Delhi, met Advani on Saturday and told him that the rebellion was being fuelled by the Congress leader Harak Singh Rawat, Leader of Opposition in the Uttarakhand Assembly.

Khanduri is also learnt to have sought disciplinary action against Koshiari. He is in Delhi since Saturday evening on a scheduled visit. He has a meeting with Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil on Monday.

Rajnath Singh is learnt to have conveyed it to the rebels that the Lok Sabha polls are just a few months away and hence, there is no question of a change in leadership at this point of time. Advani has also conveyed to Khanduri that bureaucrats cannot be allowed to act as a super chief minister in the state, said sources. The Uttarakhand BJP, meanwhile, is trying to downplay the visit of the legislators to the party headquarters in Delhi.

Party spokesperson Vishwas Dabar told The Indian Express, "These legislators had gone to Delhi to participate in the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) that was addressed by Advani on Saturday. What is the harm if they decide to meet senior party leaders on the following day. It is just a case of party members meeting their senior leaders."

The BJP has a strength of 36 legislators in the Uttarakhand Assembly and the departure of 22 legislators to Delhi has given rise to speculations in the state.

The dissidence in the state BJP has come to the fore at a crucial juncture. Uttarakhand is going in for Panchayat elections early next month and the model code of conduct has already been put into effect.

The Panchayat elections are being seen as a prelude to the Lok Sabha elections scheduled next year. The BJP leadership has been saying that it is treating the Panchayat elections as a rehearsal for the Lok Sabha polls.

Khanduri Government's popularity graph has also dipped over the last few months. The Government's decision to stall work on Bhairon Ghati and Pala Maneri power projects, following agitation by environmentalist Prof G D Aggarwal, has also drawn the ire of the locals employed at the project site.

In addition to this, Khanduri's decision to inaugurate the Srinagar Garhwal medical college in absence of state Health Minister Ramesh Pokhriyal Nishank has also not gone down well with the BJP cadres.

Heading: Post-Sachar, expert panel frames a diversity index - Indian Express
Content:
After disrupting Uttarakhand Assembly proceedings over the law and order situation in the state, Congress has now threatened to launch a statewide agitation to take its fight against "lawlessness" further.

Talking to mediapersons on Sunday morning, leader of Opposition Harak Singh Rawat said the party would begin with a token dharna at the Gandhi Park. "How can Chief Minister B C Khanduri and his administration explain the vandalism and arson by Akhil Bharati Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) activists on the premises of Garhwal and Kumaon universities last week despite the presence of a large number of police personnel?" he questioned.

Rawat said academicians from outside are reluctant to take up jobs in Uttarakhand. He said the Government and the Chief Minister were protecting the arsonists as there had been no arrests so far in these incidents. "Those rounded up by the police were also released under political pressure," said Rawat.

Referring to incidents wherein BJP leaders allegedly forced release of people from the custody of revenue police at Rudraprayag last year, a similar incident in Rudrapur and the recent incident of a BJP leader allegedly tearing up a policeman's uniform at a traffic junction in Dehradun, Rawat said a reign of terror has been let loose in the state.

"The morale of the police is at an all-time low. While the people are scared to speak out against the acts of goondaism of the BJP workers, the police too are scared to arrest them," he said.

Demanding that the state Government take immediate steps to check such acts by the BJP workers and supporters, he warned, "We are not going to be mute spectators. The police can remain quiet but we won't."

Heading: Leopard poaching on rise, 12 skins seized since July - Indian Express
Content:
Suggesting that a diversity index-based incentive and disincentive system is "more flexible" than the reservation system, an expert committee appointed by the Government to develop a Diversity Index (DI) and work out its modalities for its implementation has submitted its report.

The Government had set up the committee as a follow up to the Sachar Commission report, which had exposed definite evidence of community-based discrimination and deprivation in all social spheres. The new DI proposed by the expert committee would now form the basis for providing incentives for better representation in educational institutions, work places and living spaces.

"An incentive structure can, and should be, built into the system so that those making efforts to meet the goal of increasing diversity are rewarded. Similarly, a system of disincentives should be devised so that institutions that do not make adequate effort to increase diversity are penalised. We believe that this approach has greater flexibility than the system of reservations," the committee said in its report.

Mooting the concept of "a transparent and acceptable method to measure diversity", the EC, headed by Professor Amitabh Kundu, member, National Statistical Mission, has listed out various incentive proposals to ensure equal opportunity to all social groups in social spheres.

Giving prime focus to education, the expert committee has suggested giving incentives in the form of larger grants to those educational institutions that have higher diversity and are able to sustain it over time. These incentives can apply to both colleges and universities, both in public and private sector.

The next area of attention is the job sector. Here, the committee says that incentives should be provided to public and private sector enterprises and institutions to encourage diversity at work force. "While such initiatives should be a part of the corporate social responsibility, some affirmative action may help initiate this process, the report said.

Another area of attention is the housing sector where the panel has recommended incentives to builders for housing complexes that have more 'diverse' residents' population to promote 'composite living spaces' for 'socio-religious communities'.

Asking the Central and state governments to start designing an incentive system linked to the DI, the panel has suggested that the existing system of devolution can incorporate it as an additional criterion and even allocation of special funds can be based on this.

On the operationalisation of the DI, the panel said that the DI for an institution might be constructed by classifying the (a) workers and (b) recipients of services into a few broad grades, representing vertical hierarchy.

"The diversity indices computed for workers and recipients of services for any institution under consideration must be squared and added up for each social dimension (religion, caste and gender). The final composite DI for an institution would be worked out by obtaining a weighted average of the three indices," the report said.

According to the expert group, the responsibility of suggesting meaningful ranges of the DI for identifying diversity categories must be given to appropriate organisations at national and state levels. And based on this, institutions should be put in to three categories — those with "low diversity, mid diversity and high diversity".

Heading: Landslide near Kota claims 3,leaves 135 stranded at temple - Indian Express
Content:
In a poaching trail that covers much of North Indian leopard habitat, the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) seized a leopard skin at Vikasnagar, around 40 km from Dehradun, on August 6, taking the total number of seizures since July to 12.

It's a second case of skin seizure this month. On August 1, the bureau, along with the elite Special Operations Squad of the Delhi Crime Branch, seized a leopard skin and arrested an accused, Sandeep Sansanwal, in Delhi.

Vikasnagar, meanwhile, is emerging as a hideout for poachers. On 28 July, another leopard skin was seized at Vikasnagar in a joint operation by the Uttarakhand Special Task Force, NGO Wildlife SOS and the bureau.

The seizure also exposed a link between narcotics and wildlife crime when the accused, Yusuf, was arrested with around 300 grams of heroin in his possession. "The Uttarakhand Special Task Force had a lead on this poaching crime and they contacted us. The seizure proves that narcotics and wildlife crime go hand-in-hand, as both are high risk, high incentive," said Kartick Satyanarayan from Wildlife SOS, member of the advisory board, WCCB.

Just a day before this seizure, the UP Special Task Force on July 27 seized as many as 8 leopard skins in Saharanpur. Before that, a leopard skin was seized at Almora, Uttarakhand on 22 July.

"According to our estimates, as many as 105 leopards have been poached this year, mostly from Western Himalayas, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh," said Tito Joseph, programme manager, Wildlife Protection Society of India.

Senior WCCB officials said they were interrogating the accused. "Leopard poaching is rampant and it is part of an unorganised sector. This means poachers strike in any season though the traders and the trade routes remain the same," said Ramesh K Pandey, deputy director, WCCB.

Recent seizures

•August 6: One leopard skin seized in Vikasnagar, near Dehradun. One arrested.

•August 1: One leopard skin seized in Delhi. One held.

•July 28: One leopard skin seized. Yusuf arrested with narcotics in his possession.

•July 27: Eight leopard skins seized by UP STF in Saharanpur. Three persons arrested.

•July 22: One leopard skin seized by Uttarakhand police in Almora. Two persons held.

Heading: PDP to join separatists in ‘march’ to Muzaffarabad - Indian Express
Content:
A landslide on Sunday evening left three persons dead and more than 135 people, including 50 children and women, stranded at the Geparnath temple near Kota in Rajasthan. The exact number of people injured at the site is not known yet. Rescue operations are underway and the Army has been called in.

The temple, located around 25 km from Kota along the Chambal river, is a famous Shiv pilgrimage in the state and according to the authorities more than 1,000 people visit the site daily. The mishap occurred when a portion of the steps leading to the temple in the valley below caved in following a minor landslide earlier in the evening. The Geparnath temple and the nearby gorge is a favourite picnic and pilgrimage spot and a large number of people were present at the spot when about 15-30 steps suddenly collapsed.

According to Police officials, at least five persons may be trapped underneath the rubble and more than 200 people stranded below the temple at the picnic spot.

Though a rescue team, including 20 commandos, reached the mishap site late on Sunday night, Kota SP Vishal Bhansal told The Indian Express that rescue operations would only be started on Monday morning, as it was dangerous to move the rubble and people in the dark. He added that intermittent rains were hampering the rescue efforts.

According to the SP, food packages were dropped and a wireless contact was established with those stranded at the temple. He also said most of the rescue operations would be carried out with assistance from boat crews through the river. Two helicopters were flown down to Kota from Jaipur to assist the rescue team. A number of rock climbers and firefighters are also present to help in the rescue operations. Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje has sent Parliamentary Affairs Secretary Bhavani Singh Rajavat to the mishap site to assess the situation.

Heading: Growers’ protest ripe, parties rush in to pluck the fruits - Indian Express
Content:
In the first development of its kind in Kashmir, the mainstream People's Democratic Party has decided to join the separatists in the march to Muzaffarabad on Monday. Party president Mehbooba Mufti said its workers would constitute "a part of the main caravan" and would be led by senior leaders Abdul Aziz Zargar and Muhammad Dilawar Mir.

Mehbooba added that she was not averse to be seen alongside the secessionists on an issue that should be the common concern of every political party in the Valley. "We are fundamentally responding to the call of the fruit traders who fear that the lingering economic blockade on Kashmir would rot their produce. But if it involves sharing the stage with the separatists, we have no problem with that," she told The Indian Express. "It is our right to work with our people in search of an alternative trading route. If Punjab can trade across the Wagah-Attari border, why not Kashmir?"

The Hurriyat, however, rejected the PDP's move to participate in the march. "We know what they are up to. It is sheer vote bank politics for them. If they try to join us, they will not be welcome," Hurriyat chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, who claimed to have been placed under house arrest on Sunday, a day ahead of the march, told The Indian Express. He added that it was the PDP that was responsible for the present crisis. "It is the party that gave the land in the first place". Hardline separatist Syed Ali Shah Geelani is already under house arrest for the past six days.

PDP's arch rival National Conference has steered clear of the march, limiting itself to expressing concern over the continuing blockade.

The PDP hopes to use the march to straddle the Valley's mainstream-separatist divide and thereby appeal to a wider votebank. However, the reaction to its decision is a matter of speculation, given the wide belief that it was party to the land allotment to the Amarnath shrine board, which sparked off the crisis.

Mehbooba said she was not concerned about the signals a PDP leader sharing the stage with the hardline Geelani would send. "We are usually accused in India of having a nexus with the militants. And in Kashmir we are seen as a staunch pro-India party," she said. "So we can't hold ourselves hostage to perceptions." However, she added, the PDP had not arrived at any understanding with the separatists on the issue.

Senior PDP leader and former J-K finance minister Tariq Hameed Karra said the PDP was acting on what were its own views. "The demand for opening up of the cross-LoC routes is our brainchild. Others have merely followed. So what is wrong if we are translating our agenda into action?" Karra said. He added that the PDP's idea of a dual currency in the entire J-K was most relevant now. "We want economic integration with India, Pakistan and the rest of the world. Access is our birthright."

Heading: Jammu protests during curfew, shops when it’s lifted - Indian Express
Content:
The fruit growers here are watching in dismay as separatists and political parties with their own agendas hijack their march towards the Line of Control.

The leadership of the growers has been formally conveyed by followers of Syed Ali Shah Geelani to follow his march programme on Monday and told that the procession would be led by the Hurriyat hardliner himself instead of the fruit growers' leaders.

This morning, as leaders of fruit growers were giving final touches to the cross-LoC march at the Sopore fruit mandi, Geelani's emissaries dropped in with the message. Since the National Highway was blocked, the Sopore fruit mandi has presented a deserted look, but today hundreds of growers had assembled to chalk out a strategy for the march. Many growers were distributing pamphlets and arranging vehicles for the procession.

A majority of growers are opposed to the Hurriyat jumping onto their bandwagon as, for them, the march is more an economic rather than a political issue. "We are traders and don't want to play politics," Ghulam Rasool Bhat, President, Fruit Growers' and Dealers' Association, said.

Bhat added that every Kashmiri could join the march towards the LoC in his individual capacity. "We don't want to make it a political event or a platform for separatists," he said. "The aim of this march is to highlight faces of communal elements in India who are destroying our fruit industry."

In fact, to keep the march away from politics, the growers had even constituted a coordination committee to lead the procession, with members from different trade bodies who have no affiliation with any political or separatist group. "Ours is a non-political march," said Ghulam Rasool Wagay, Secretary, All Valley Fruit Growers' Association, one of the members of the coordination committee. "We are taking this extreme step to save our fruit industry that is worth thousands of crores."

Earlier, on Friday, fruit growers had refused a Hurriyat appeal to change their programme of crossing the LoC. Later, both factions of the Hurriyat had clubbed their programme with the fruit growers' march.

"We will start marching towards Muzaffarabad from every village," General Secretary, Sopore fruit mandi, Ghulam Mohammad Malik said. "We will take our fruit in trucks, load carriers and in private vehicles as we have been forced to take this extreme step."

Heading: Govt trucks sent back empty - Indian Express
Content:
Jammu is witnessing a strange trend. While those protesting against revocation of the land transfer order have no qualms about defying the curfew for protests, there are hardly any protests when the curfew is actually relaxed.

"It is amusing. Normal life returns to the city when the curfew is relaxed, but when it is re-imposed, the same people, who were till then busy shopping, join protest rallies defying the curfew,"' said a police officer. "I think the administration should extend the relaxation to calm the people," he added. The district has been under curfew for the last seven days with relaxation from 5 to 9 am.

"The people are fixing up their day-to-day schedule very cleverly during the curfew," said an Major on duty at Canal Road. "During the relaxation hours they prefer to shop for essential goods than to protest. As soon as the curfew is re-imposed, the protestors take to the streets again," he added.

The protestors, however, say this is intentional. Participating in a peaceful protest rally in the area, Vikas Gupta of Trikuta Nagar said: "We are intentionally moving out during the curfew to show the administration that we are protesting against the bias shown against the region and the curfew imposed here."

Heading: Sinha breaks silence:PDP anti-national - Indian Express
Content: With the fruit growers threatening to march to Muzaffarabad on Monday with their produce, the Government on Sunday lined up 96 trucks at Sopore fruit mandi — the country's second largest — to help them transport the fruits. However, the growers refused to load their produce in the vehicles. "We have no faith in the Government as they don't care for us," said the mandi's General Secretary, Ghulam Mohammad Malik. Police have been deputed in and outside the fruit mandi that is becoming the focal point of the march. Area Marketing Officer, Sopore Mandi, Fayaz Ahmad said the growers had suffered heavy losses since the disruption of the highway. Every year around two crore fruit boxes are dispatched to different fruit markets of the country from this mandi.  Since the protests began, say growers, they have lost Rs 500 crore. Fruit selling is Kashmir's largest trade, with three million people directly or indirectly associated with it.

Heading: Rlys tells devotees to keep off Vaishno Devi - Indian Express
Content:
Terming the controversy over the revocation of land transfer order to the Sri Amarnath Shrine Board (SASB) as a national tragedy, former Jammu and Kashmir governor Lt General S K Sinha (retd) has said the transfer of land was not an unusual decision as huge tracts of forest land have been transferred for various purposes, including starting hydel project, setting up communication towers and starting educational institutes.

He was delivering a keynote address at a seminar 'Shri Amarnath Land Transfer — Implications of Revocation', organised by the Forum on Integrated National Security, Chandigarh, on Sunday.

Calling the People's Democratic Party anti-national, former J-K governor said, "The Valley is inhabitated by 45 per cent Kashmiri Muslims, around 35 per cent Hindus and Sikhs and some Christians, 20 per cent Gujjars and Bakerwals and 2 to 3 per cent Buddhists." The PDP had been trying to create a rift, he added.

Listing out measures needed to control the situation, Lt Gen Sinha said, "There should be no appeasement of any faction while dealing with the situation. The people of Jammu should be requested to refrain from violence to prevent communal enmity. Checks need to be imposed on forces trying to stop essential supplies from entering Kashmir. The facts about land transfer must be made clear to the people."

Having received flak from various quarters and blamed for being party to the decision, Lt Gen Sinha said he felt it was his duty to go around the country and apprise people of what the facts were. "It was in 2005 that the request for transfer of land to the Shrine Board was made. With the approval of the Cabinet and pressures from ministers the land was transferred. The SASB had been putting up pre-fabricated structures for the convenience of pilgrims. The area in Baltal can be accessed only for three to four months a year. The rest of the year there it is heavy snowfall. Due to the structures tourism in the area increased," he says.

Noted commentator Saeed Naqvi presented a documentary film made by him on various religious places in the country. It depicted how cutting across religious barriers, temples and mosques were being maintained by people from other religions.

President of the forum P C Dogra, former DGP Punjab, said the long hidden frustration of the people was coming to surface in the Valley. It is a stage-managed show by separatists and some segments of mainstream politics.

Heading: Malik ends fast - Indian Express
Content:
Due to the Amarnath land row in the Jammu region, devotees headed for Vaishno Devi have been advised both by the Indian Railways Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) and Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board to abstain from visiting the temple.

While in July, the number of devotees visiting the temple on the IRCTC weekly packages reduced to 110 from 144 in June, in August, not a single person took either of the two packages which were scheduled to leave on August 1 and 8. In a month, there are four packages of 36 seats each.

Heading: Farmers protest ‘land grab’, Maya village turns fortress - Indian Express
Content:
Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF) chairman Mohammad Yaseen Malik on Sunday ended his six-day-long fast unto death following a message from Prime Minister Manmohan Singh requesting him to end the fast. Malik took a glass of juice from the mother of one of the youths, Asif Mehraj, who was killed in police action while protesting against the economic blockade in the Valley at Maisuma on Monday.

Suicide attempt

JAMMU: Protesting against the revocation of transfer of land to the Shri Amarnath Shrine Board (SASB), a youth Anil Kumar Sharma attempted suicide by consuming pesticides on Sunday .He was rushed to the Government Medical College (GMC) hospital.

Heading: Denied elbow room by Maya, Ajit in a fix - Indian Express
Content:
Sealed from all sides, Badalpur village, nearly 35 km from Delhi and better known as UP Chief Minister Mayawati's parental village, resembled a fortress on Sunday. With Samajwadi Party (SP) leaders threatening to enter the village to support farmers of the Kisan Sangharsh Committee protesting against the rate of compensation offered by the Mayawati Government for acquiring nearly 400 hectare of land in the area. About 100 police personnel deployed by the Noida police kept vigil throughout the day.

Nearly 800 farmers from Badalpur and three other villages — Bishnuli, Sadulpur and Achenja — have been protesting against the state Government's step to acquire land for developing a green belt of 400 hectare around a recreation centre being built by Mayawati on a property spread across 47 bighas in the village. While Badalpur alone contributes 230 hectare, the other three contribute around 170 hectare. While the Government is offering the farmers Rs 711 per square metre, they claim that the market rate is Rs 4,500-5,000 per square metre.

"There was no permission to hold any demonstration or agitation in the area so we had to impose restrictions. We had deployed police personnel and vans on all routes leading to the village right from the Delhi-UP border," said SSP R K Chaturvedi, adding that the police arrested four MPs and three MLAs of the SP near Ghazipur Sabzi Mandi. The SP leaders taken into custody included Dharmendar Yadav, Ashok Chauhan and Madan Chauhan amongst others.

While the administration met with the agitating group of about 200-odd farmers to find a solution, the situation remained tense with talks being scheduled for Tuesday. Meanwhile, the Sangharsh Committee has said the farmers will not ally with any political party.

Jasvir Numberdar, the head of the agitating group, said, "This is our fight with the administration and Mayawati because they are taking our land by paying less and not offering any employment security. We do not want any support from any political party."

With the Congress and BSP drifting apart after the former joined hands with Mulayam Singh Yadav and the third front declaring Mayawati as the leader, the protesting farmers have found support from both the Congress and SP.

The Noida police had earlier foiled a protest rally planned by the Congress to support the agitating farmers by arresting Congress general secretary Digvijay Singh, party MP Sachin Pilot and UPCC president Rita Bahuguna Joshi on July 29 at the Delhi-UP border when they were on their way to join a rally organised by the protesting committee.

Triggered by the Congress support and agitation on July 29, the Government has now set up base camps to give out the compensation for the land. According to the figures given by the Dadri Tehsil, 575 of the 800 farmers have come forward so far.

BSP's district head Kartar Singh whose residence alone was fortified by about 25 police personnel, said, "The agitation is unjustified as it is being fuelled by rival parties and the property dealer lobby. We are convincing people to come forward."

Heading: Blasts take place whenever BJP is in trouble: Digvijay - Indian Express
Content:
Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) chief Ajit Singh has been left in the lurch following BSP supremo Mayawati's declaration at her Lucknow rally on Saturday that she has finalised candidates for all the 80 Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh.

Singh had joined hands with Mayawati to vote against the UPA trust motion, hoping to clinch an electoral alliance with the BSP in the Lok Sabha polls. But now it seems Mayawati has chosen to elbow out Singh, leaving him with no other option but to either align with the SP-Congress combine or go alone and endanger his political future.

Mayawati's declaration also comes as a jolt to the Left parties plan of building a rainbow coalition comprising UNPA and other parties as a viable alternative to the UPA and NDA.

Though Singh could not be contacted, RLD's Dalit MP Munsi Ram lamented Mayawati's decision. "What can we do? Our leader Ajit Singh had extended an opportunity to Mayawati to change the socio-political fabric of Uttar Pradesh, but it seems she is not interested," Ram told The Indian Express.

Party sources said that Singh had already opened back-channel talks with the Congress leadership fearing that Mayawati could ditch him since her aim of toppling the UPA Government during the trust vote had failed. Congress sources confirmed that the RLD leader was sending feelers to them.

Though it was learnt that both the Congress and the SP were keen to accommodate Singh in a bid to improve their poll prospects in UP, it remains to be seen how they accept him in the changed scenario. "Earlier, Congress and SP were wooing us. But now we need them," said an RLD leader.

Ajit Singh is reported to have sought the help of Left parties too, to mediate with Mayawati. Singh paid a visit to the CPI(M) office on Thursday and met senior party leaders. The Left leaders had played a role in getting the RLD against the UPA. But now it appears that they too have given up on Mayawati.

The UP Chief Minister made her intentions clear when she announced candidates on seats the RLD could not afford to part with like Mathura (from where Singh wants his son to contest), Bagpat (Singh's constituency) and Kairana, all in the Jat land of western UP-Singh's turf.

Heading: Buffalo milk vs cow milk, MP has a fat problem - Indian Express
Content:
Apparently taking a cue from Sushma Swaraj, AICC general secretary Digvijay Singh on Sunday claimed serial blasts occur in India only when the BJP is in trouble. Soon after the serial blasts in Ahmedabad and Bangalore, Swaraj had accused the UPA Government of masterminding the blasts to divert the attention of people from the horsetrading of MPs for the trust vote.

"Serial blasts occurred in Bangalore and Ahmedabad soon after the BJP's defeat in the July-22 trust vote," said Singh. Demanding a probe into the blasts, the AICC general secretary in charge of party affairs in UP said, "It should be thoroughly investigated who was behind the blasts and who masterminded the conspiracy."

Addressing the first meeting of the newly constituted UP Congress Committee executive, Singh said: "People should take cognisance of the fact that the blasts took place when the BJP was in trouble. Whenever the BJP is in trouble, bomb blasts take place in the country. When the Tehelka issue rocked the House, Parliament was attacked, Jaipur blasts took place when the Karnataka elections were on and recently when the BJP's trust motion was defeated bomb blasts took place in Ahmedabad and Bangalore".

Holding the Sangh Parivar responsible for the blasts, the former Madhya Pradesh chief minister said: "It is intriguing that in Surat bombs were found on trees. I have evidence to prove that the persons owing allegiance to the RSS and VHP were involved in making and planting the bombs." He added that fanatics of both communities were involved in terrorism.

Singh demanded a probe by the Union Home Ministry into UP Chief Minister Mayawati's claims that there was a threat to her life.

Heading: ‘CBI, the Tom, will catch Q, the Jerry, one day’ - Indian Express
Content:
It's A fight between faith and fat. The face-off is between the Madhya Pradesh Commission for the Poor Among General Category, which has faith in cow's milk for its medicinal properties, and the state's Dairy Federation, which is all for buffalo's milk, with more fat content.

The debate started over the Acharya Vidyasagar Gau Samvardhan Yojana, under which 10,000 potential beneficiaries will get two cows each, free of cost, with the Government providing for fodder and even taking the responsibility to market the milk.

A meeting between the commission and federation officials to give final touches to the ambitious scheme, announced by the Government to milk votes in an election year, met its first hurdle over fat content. The federation insisted that the demand and market for buffalo's milk was more due to the heavy fat content.

When the commission learnt that cow's milk would be mixed with buffalo's and then sold, its chairman Babulal Jain put his foot down. "Cow's milk is the elixir of life. Those who consume it become energetic and smart unlike buffalo's milk, which produces lazy people," the septuagenarian chairman of the commission told The Indian Express on Saturday.

Such arguments are not new in BJP-ruled Madhya Pradesh. Since the party wrested power from the Congress in 2003, all its three chief ministers—Uma Bharati, Babulal Gaur and Shivraj Singh Chouhan—have harped on a cow-based economy.

"If they don't have a separate network for marketing cow's milk it's their problem," the former education minister said, adding that he was also exploring the possibility of tying up with some NGOs. He says the two bovine species can't be talked in the same breath because the cow has a special status in Indian culture. "Cow urine and dung have special medicinal uses."

"We can't create a market for cow's milk if it does not exist. We won't be able to market it," countered the federation. They insist buffalo's milk carries more fat and, hence, earns more money. Incidentally, the Indian Dairy Federation roots for buffalo's milk because it's commercially more viable and because there is a difference in nutritive value.

The Commission for the Poor Among General Category was set up by the MP Government in February with the former education minister as its head. Setting a record of sorts, Jain had submitted his report within 100 days after travelling to nearly two-dozen districts and talking to the rural poor.

At a massive gathering in the last week of June, the Chief Minister had made several announcements for the economically backward people in general category.

From free cows to free textbooks and from free education in state-run professional colleges to the government standing guarantee to loans for higher education, the government had promised something for all sections.

The free cows were meant for women, the neglected section of the general category. One thousand women each will be selected from ten divisions of the state under the scheme. The beneficiaries will be able to buy the animals from melas that will be specially organised for them.

Heading: Manmohan natural choice as PM, too early for Rahul: Pawar - Indian Express
Content:
The 'Jerry' in Italian businessman Ottavio Quattrocchi, one of the key accused in the long running Bofors case, may have outsmarted the CBI several times, but the 'Tom' in the agency is waiting for its chance.

The CBI has drawn a parallel between the Bofors case and the popular cartoon show — Tom and Jerry — and is hopeful that 'Tom' will one day catch 'Jerry'.

"I like Tom and Jerry cartoon show and the police is like the cat while the criminals are like mice. So, Tom never leaves Jerry," newly appointed CBI Director Ashwani Kumar has said in response to a question whether the agency will give up its pursuit of Quattrocchi.

Quattrocchi, who was detained in Malaysia and released last in Argentina, is wanted by the CBI in the Rs 64-crore Bofors kickback scam of early 1990s.

To a question whether the CBI had drawn a blank in seeking his extradition from the two countries after lengthy legal battles, the CBI Director said, "I am in the game of Tom and Jerry and I have to do my job."

To a question that a substantial amount of taxpayers' money had been spent on the case and that if the time had come to wind it up, Kumar said, "I have a particular role to perform — corrupt fellows run away from the police and I have to catch them. This role I will continue to do." "Our role is to catch criminals involved in scams and bring them before law," Kumar, a 1973 batch IPS officer from Himachal cadre, said.

Heading: Faith in Sonia, but won’t be in Cabinet: Rane - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh appears a natural choice as the PM candidate of the UPA in the next elections and it may be "too early" for Rahul Gandhi, NCP supremo and a key UPA partner Sharad Pawar has suggested. He also favours the UPA unitedly contesting the coming Assembly elections in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan and Delhi to send the right message ahead of the Lok Sabha elections.

"Congress as the major party in the UPA has to take a call on the leadership issue. It should decide and discuss with the allies....but if we want someone who is non-controversial then Manmohan Singh is there," Pawar told PTI in an interview.

He made it clear that "it is too early to say anything" about the leadership of Rahul Gandhi, projected by the Congress as a potential leader and a future Prime Minister.

The NCP chief is the first among the UPA leaders to pitch for Manmohan as PM candidate. He had expressed a similar view sometime back after which some Congress leaders like Arjun Singh had attempted to project Rahul Gandhi, drawing instant snub from the party high command.

Pawar feels the Lok Sabha elections will be held at the scheduled time in March-April next year.

He does not see the possibility of the UPA going for early polls by the year-end after a record foodgrains production and possible reining in of inflation in the next few months.

Answering a range of questions including the state of affairs in the national parties, especially the Congress, the Amarnath issue and the rise of the regional parties, the Union Agriculture Minister said the 15th Lok Sabha could turn out to be a short affair if either Congress or the BJP failed to win a minimum of 150 seats and form the next Government. "In the coming elections, it will be difficult for any party to get 160-170 seats."

Heading: Boys’ deaths: Asaram’s son under CID scanner - Indian Express
Content:
Maharashtra Revenue Minister Narayan Rane on Sunday vowed his loyalty to Congress president Sonia Gandhi and the party even as he maintained he was not ready to continue in Vilasrao Deshmukh's Cabinet under any circumstances.

"I have full faith in Madam. I am sure she knows what I am doing is only for the interest of the people and the party. I will go by her decision," Rane told The Indian Express over telephone from Mumbai. He, however, clarified he was not contemplating to leave the party as yet.

"The Congress president knows everything. She knows what is in public interest and what is not. Whenever she calls me, I will go and explain everything. I will take any decision (about future course) only after that. I will not quit the party, but I will not be a minister. While staying in the party, I will see how Vilasrao Deshmukh does his best to bring the Shiv Sena-BJP back to power in Maharashtra," said Rane.

Earlier, he had sent two letters to the Congress President: one exposing the functioning and non-performance of the Deshmukh Government and the other being a copy of resignation letter addressed to the Governor. He was, however, silent on whether he had sent the said resignation letter to the Governor.

The Congress president is likely to take a call on the issue this week. While the party has officially disapproved and distanced itself from Rane's outburst against Deshmukh Cabinet's decision to allot prime land to Videocon recently, a section of the Congress remains sympathetic with Rane "so far as issues he is raising are concerned". They put a question mark on Deshmukh regime for the "haste" it showed in the latest land allotment.

"As for his Government's performance, be it drought management or tackling incidence of suicide or the minority community's demands on Srikrishna Commission report, the lesser said the better. But Rane cannot go about publicising it. He should be a little diplomatic; he does not know the CM's links in the party," said an AICC general secretary.

Another senior leader said while the NCP continued to gain ground during the NCP-Congress rule, the Congress has only been losing its base as is evident from recent elections. As for Deshmukh's "links" in New Delhi, sources pointed out how former PCC chief Prabha Rau, who had taken up cudgels against the CM on account of his regime's perceived non-performance, was shunted out of the party as Governor. Margaret Alva, the AICC general secretary in charge of Maharashtra, who had supported Rau, also looks set to be divested of the state's charge, said sources.

Asked about the party's disapproval of his public outbursts against Deshmukh, Rane said: "I cannot keep my mouth shut if anybody compromises public interest. Nobody can justify the decision to give a piece of land (to a company) for Rs 300 crore even though its market price is up to Rs 4,000 to 5,000 crore. Under Vilasrao Deshmukh's leadership, the people of Maharashtra have got only load shedding, suicide, unemployment and drought but the Chief Minister has no time for their problems. He is busy serving his own interests. I will not work under Deshmukh's leadership."

Sources said the party High Command was not inclined to change the Chief Minister at this stage. All that the party leadership is prepared to offer Rane are some olive branches, including the post of PCC chief/Campaign Committee chairperson, and two ministries and two boards for Rane's supporters. Although he has declined these offers so far insisting on Deshmukh's removal, the party leadership is unlikely to oblige.

The three-member panel set up to solve the Maharashtra imbroglio—including External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee, Defence Minister AK Antony and Ahmed Patel, Political Secretary to the Congress president—is learnt to be divided on this issue.

Heading: Students suffer in poll haste to get IIT-Patna off ground - Indian Express
Content:
In the latest development in the investigations into the mysterious deaths of two minor children from the Asaram Ashram-run gurukul in Ahmedabad, the Criminal Investigation Department (Crime) on Sunday summoned Asaram Bapu's son, Narayan Sindhi, to appear before the investigating officer.

Sindhi, who stays at an ashram in Sabarkantha district, was informed through a fax message to appear before the CID in two days.

Investigating Officer H B Rajput said: "A lot of things have been appearing in local dailies alleging that Narayan Sindhi is involved in exorcist activities. Following this, we decided to call him for questioning to see if he has any role in the deaths of the two children," said Rajput.

He added, "So far, we do not have any evidence against him."

The mutilated bodies of the two boys, Dipesh and Abhishek, were found from the Sabarmati riverbed on July 5, two days after they mysteriously disappeared from the ashram.

Postmortem report suggested that the internal organs of one of the boys were missing. Parents of both boys have been alleging that their sons had been killed by the ashram authorities as part of some 'black magic' ritual.

The case was handed over to the CID following public agitations in the city.

Heading: Jammu, Kashmir integral part of India: Advani - Indian Express
Content:
In an election year where symbolism matters, what could be more symbolic than getting one of the most sought-after institutes of excellence to the capital of a state many have given up on? That perhaps explains the haste with which IIT-Patna was inaugurated on August 6. The building was only half ready and even Union Human Resources Development Minister Arjun Singh pulled out of the function due to ill-health, but an access road sprang up overnight as an eager administration pressed ahead.

IIT-Patna is only one of two new IITs launched from an independent campus this year, one step forward in the HRD Ministry's aim of six new IITs this year. India currently has seven IITs, and the Ministry hopes to add eight more. Besides Bihar, new IITs are supposed to start this academic session in Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Orissa, Gujarat and Punjab. IIT-Rajasthan, Punjab and Orissa will operate from the existing campuses of IIT Kanpur, Delhi and Mumbai. Patna and Gandhinagar IITs have to put up with temporary campuses. Till IIT Patna gets parliamentary ratification, it will work as an extension of IIT Guwahati, which will 'mentor' it.

Bogged down by infrastructure constraints, running on a leased campus and functioning with borrowed faculty from 'mentor' IIT-Guwahati, IIT- Patna is struggling to even provide basic amenities to the 108 students who have enrolled for its 120 seats.

It is also the "dilution" of academic standards that many are alarmed about. Contrary to the HRD Ministry's claims about the massive IIT expansion not impacting teaching quality, the figures speak for themselves. While the teacher-pupil ratio at IITs is ideally between 1:9 and 1:10, at IIT-Patna it is nearly 1:13 or 1:14.

The teachers are also strictly in the nature of visiting faculty and will complete a semester of the course — six months or so — and then return to IIT-Guwahati. Halfway down the academic session a new set of faculty members will join.

While he insists that these are teething problems, not very different from the ones faced by other IITs, IIT- Guwahati Director Gautam Barua who is also in-charge of the Patna campus says: "It would have definitely been better if we had a few months more of preparation time."

While the management will soon put out advertisements to build a core faculty for IIT-Patna, it is no secret that getting IIT-grade faculty is a feat by itself. "We will be advertising for 30 faculty positions and laboratory staff positions almost immediately and we are hoping that we will manage to get at least 15-20 faculty members by next month," says Prof S Dandapat, Dean, IIT-Patna.

Sources say the HRD Ministry was so keen on starting IIT-Patna this academic session itself that the state Government had to hurriedly look for a temporary set-up this March and were lucky enough to find a two-storey building under construction at the 10,000-sq ft Polytechnic campus. A third floor to house the laboratories was also planned, but the inauguration announcement came before it could be completed.

IIT-Patna's permanent campus is at least three years and 25 km away, at Bihta. The state Science and Technology Department officials say procurement of land is at an advanced stage. "We are preparing a hydrological profile of the site," said an official.

The Polytechnic building has its own shortfalls, which begin with it being located in a low-lying area that becomes waterlogged every rainfall. While the ground floor houses the faculty, staff offices and a canteen, and the second floor five classrooms and two halls, the IIT will get its laboratories, library and more classrooms only in another three months when the third floor is ready. Until then it has to depend on the Polytechnic's laboratories. There is also a severe shortage of computers.

However, IIT-Guwahati Director Barua is categorical that these are not "handicaps". "When an institute begins, there will be some teething troubles. I should know, as I was at IIT- Guwahati when the first batch joined," he replied to The Indian Express in an e-mail. Barua instead praised the Bihar Government for being "very cooperative" in providing basic infrastructure. "Frankly speaking, we could not have asked for more."

While some of the temporary faculty members have complained about lack of accommodation facilties, forcing them to share rooms in a flat, Barua calls these too initial problems. "We started IIT-Guwahati in a similar manner, in fact in much worse conditions. IIMs, IISERs, all are being started in a similar manner. Yes, faculty are sharing flats, their families are not here. Girl students have been put in a flat next to the faculty. We have hired more flats and when IIT-Patna faculty join, they will be given individual flats."

He is hopeful of this happening soon, if not immediately, and adds that there are enough faculty right now to teach the courses. "The issue of ratios has no meaning in the first few semesters. What will more faculty from Guwahati do? We have advertised for faculty posts. We don't really need 30 to run the programme in the first year," he says.

Students, many of whom admit IIT- Patna was their last choice, don't hide their disappointment. Says Sai V Reddy, a student from Andhra Pradesh: "There has to be a library at the institute and a playground and plenty of indoor and outdoor games facilities." Udaiveer, who has come from Rajasthan, wonders why there was so much hurry to start the IIT without any preparation.

The parent of Prajjwal from Sonepat, Prem Kumar Sharma, was concerned about the vast gap between IIT-Patna and the other established IITs.

Dean Samarendra Dandapat, however, puts up a brave face. Attending to the two landlines in his office that ring almost incessantly, he says this is how IITs start, and there is "all-round enthusiasm among everyone".

Heading: RBI searches 628 bank branches in UP for fake currency notes - Indian Express
Content:
After hardselling Amarnath as the party's new-found symbol of "territorial integrity and cultural nationalism," BJP's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani on Sunday claimed that "those opposed to the Amarnath land transfer were questioning Jammu and Kashmir's status as an integral part of the country".

"Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India; whoever raises questions on this issue will have to pay for it," he said at a function to release the special issue of a children's magazine dedicated to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

"This is not a question of Amarnath or a shrine alone. They are saying it is okay that you have alloted land for Vaishno Devi in Jammu but how can you allot land in Kashmir," said BJP's prime ministerial candidate.

Advani, who, as the National Democratic Alliance leader, has been mum on the party's pet agenda of abrogation of Article 370 (according Jammu and Kashmir a special status) recalled the Bharatiya Jana Sangh ideologue Shyama Prasad Mookerjee's role in the state's integration with the country.

"Shyama Prasad Mookerjee, during his struggle 55 years ago for cancelling the visa system for those visiting the state, had promised people that he would either get the permit system abolished or sacrifice his life ... we seem to have turned a full circle today," he said.

On Saturday, Advani, at a Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha rally, had said that "every Indian has the right on every inch of land and that no one could question allotment of land for Amarnath pilgrims in the Valley".

Heading: Why the Forces not be with Patil - Indian Express
Content: The all-party meeting to discuss the Jammu stalemate proved to be a marathon four-hour affair. But it was essentially due to regional parties, which used the meeting to peddle their own agenda. While the Asom Gana Parishad's Brindaban Goswami used the occasion to highlight the infiltration issue in his state, and demanded a similar exercise to discuss the problem, others like the PMK and Shiv Sena sang paeans to their respective leaders. The dialogue that fructified in an appeal for peace in the state was essentially between the Congress, BJP and the two Kashmir-based parties, the PDP and NC.

Heading: India’s answer to Tibet rail: PMO clears plan for train to Leh via Rohtang - Indian Express
Content: The tendency of the Home Ministry to throw up its hands and call in the Army to handle internal disturbances is not going down well with the Defence Ministry. At one point during the ongoing Jammu crisis, when more paramilitary was needed, Home Minister Shivraj Patil simply told the Cabinet Committee on Security that he did not have any paramilitary to spare and that the Army should undertake responsibilities. While the Army did move in, Defence Minister A K Antony, prompted by his ministry, conveyed his discomfiture to the Prime Minister about calling in the Army in such large numbers to carry out law and order duties for which they are not adequately trained. It was finally decided that the Army will focus only on keeping lines of communication open, essentially the National Highway,  while the Home Ministry arranged for more paramilitary.

Heading: Musharraf’s own ask him to go, PPP says he gobbled $700 m - Indian Express
Content:
In what is seen as India's response to China's Tibet Rail, the Prime Minister's Office has given its in-principle approval to Himachal Pradesh's proposal for a railway line to Leh via the Rohtang Pass. The high-powered China Study Group (CSG) has been asked to provide its assessment by the month-end.

Simultaneously, the PMO has already instructed the Railway Ministry to carry out a proper feasibility survey of the Bilaspur-Leh route and submit its report latest by November. Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, sources said, is keen that there should be no delay in taking the proposal forward.

The CSG that comprises the Foreign Secretary, Defence Secretary, Home Secretary besides heads of the Intelligence Bureau and RAW will now look into the project from a strategic perspective and give its comments by August-end. A favourable opinion from the CSG will elevate the strategic significance of the project and remove several funding barriers.

The plan on paper is to build a railway line from Bilaspur to Leh covering approximately 400 km which, by a broad estimate, could end up costing around Rs 5,000 crore. Already, the Centre has agreed to provide Rs 1,000 crore for building the railway line from Bhanupalli to Bilaspur which can be then extended further.

Similarly, Rs 1,300 crore has been sanctioned for gauge conversion of the Pathankot-Jogindernagar railway line. The larger plan is that this line would intersect with the Bilaspur line that would carry on to Leh via the Rohtang Pass.

In all, the Centre is backing the Himachal government to build about 650 km of railway lines in the state which will have major strategic and economic significance. Currently, the broad estimate is that about Rs 8,000-10,000 crore will have to budgeted for this purpose.

Now that the PMO has given its nod, sources said, the various proposals would move faster with considerable pressure being brought on the Railways to carry out the requisite technical work.

China began its work on the Qinghai-Tibet railway more than two decades ago. Unlike this case, the Chinese had to build 1,956 km and the first stretch rom Qinghai to Golmund was built by 1984 while the all-important and challenging 1,142 km Golmund-Lhasa line was inaugurated only two years ago.

India is already working on an ambitious railway line into the Kashmir Valley. Top officials say the projects in Himachal Pradesh must also be taken up without delay so that connectivity can be provided to the strategically important Ladakh region.

The push has come from the state government that has been lobbying hard with the Centre on these projects. In fact, Himachal CM Prem Kumar Dhumal made a strong plea in writing to President Pratibha Patil during her visit to the state two months ago.

Heading: Basketball the next football? Beijing sets the ball rolling - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan President Pervez Musharraf today faced mounting pressure from friends and foes to quit as the ruling coalition prepared a "comprehensive and solid" chargesheet to nail him in an impeachment motion to be brought in the National Assembly session starting tomorrow.

Firing a fresh salvo, ruling PPP chief Asif Ali Zardari accused Musharraf, who has often targeted the country's politicians for indulging in corruption, of misappropriation of $700 million of anti-terror aid provided by the US.

Cracks have already appeared in Musharraf's main ally PML(Q) with MP Sardar Bahadur Khan Sihar advising the President to gracefully quit and claiming to have "support" of a dozen MPs. Four FATA senators have also asked Musharraf to quit.

Heading: On the table, a way out: go by law on shrine board powers, court rulings - Indian Express
Content:
There is a theory, much cited but of apocryphal provenance, that basketball too was invented in China. It is, they say, akin to the ancient Chinese ball-game of shouju.

The veracity of the theory is not the point. If there be no connection to basketball from ancient China, we could just recast that one-liner about cricket in India and say, basketball is a Chinese game accidentally invented in America.

To gauge the Chinese affinity for basketball, don't look only at the growing viewership for live NBA broadcasts, or at what was billed as the most watched basketball match in history when China took on the US tonight, with President George W Bush in attendance.

Consider just an aspiration.

When the conceptual design of the Wukesong Stadium, the basketball venue for the Beijing Games, went to Swiss architecture firm Burckhardt + Partner, the plan was to have a cubic structure, with massive LCD screens on all four sides, displaying outside the action within. But, according to the architecture journal FuturArc, considerations of cost and light pollution forced abandonment of the screens. Never mind, the ambition counts.

And if local buzz that the game tonight would get an audience of a billion appears un-falsifiable, find the confirmation in the number-crunching instinct of pure commerce. "NBA China has just appointed a CEO who used be CEO of Microsoft China," informs basketball writer Alexander Wolff. "That tells you something."

Wolff, author of Big Game, Small World: A Basketball Adventure, says this is the second big Olympic moment for the game. In 1992, he says, Barcelona launched the profile of football. Three years earlier, the International Amateur Basketball Federation had cleared the participation of NBA professional players in the Summer Games, and America's Dream Team set a standard for glamour and arrogant excellence unmatched in team sport at the Olympics. These Games, he argues, will confirm the profile of basketball in China.

Is basketball becoming the next football? The sport that draws interest and aspiration from the city sidewalks, that engages diverse societies in conversation, that's getting the big bucks?

This summer, just three-four weeks ago, the Iranian basketball team was invited by the NBA to train in Utah. This summer too, amidst growing US-Iran tension over Tehran's nuclear programme, there's been debate too about a direct American conversation with Iran. But "NBA has been quickest and smartest at recognizing opportunity," says Wolff. It's business, he notes, but it's also a projection of what political scientists call soft power.

Wolff says he was amazed to see a playground to the east of Tiananmen Square, with five full basketball courts, the other day. He spotted eight-nine NBA jerseys, each of them different. (The reference is to the various teams in the NBA league.) The global spread of basketball, he notes, is reflected in more ways. In the march of athletes at the opening ceremony on Friday, five non-American flag-bearers were NBA players — including, of course, China's Yao Ming who plays with the Houston Rockets.

The internationalisation of basketball bears benefits for the NBA too. "It has changed the style of play for the better," says Wolff. There was too much one-on-one play. The international game, with the infusion of foreign players like Yao, Germany's Dirk Nowitzk and Argentina's Manu Ginobili into the NBA, has brought more fluid passes and ball movement.

For America, 2004 was a disaster. Many top players did not show up for the team, and the US went home with the bronze. After that, says Wolff, the focus has been on revitalizing the composition and attitude of the team. With three years spent building a team for the Olympics, and with the emergence of the post-Michael Jordan group of superstars like Kobe Bryant and LeBron James, the outlook is again good.

But perhaps that American slip, with Argentina taking the gold and Italy the silver, has given the rest deeper hope.

It is interesting to note that when that vote on allowing NBA professionals to play at the Olympics was taken, the US dissented. The impression was that international matches would be so lopsided that there'd be no viewer interest. Tonight's big match will banish that fear forever.

Heading: Hurriyat stronger after row, Kashmir admn tells team led by Patil - Indian Express
Content:
The Amarnath shrine land transfer row, which has paralysed Jammu and Kashmir for two months, today seemed to have moved a step towards a possible resolution. One way out, already being called the most viable, has incidentally come from a BJP national leader — a solution which calls for adherence to the Shri Amarnath Shrine Board Act and court interpretations of the Act outlining the powers and functions of the Board.

"Stick to two things: the Shri Amarnath Shrine Board Act, a legislation passed by the J&K Legislative Assembly in 2000, that led to the formation of Amarnath Shrine Board and the court directions interpreting its powers and functions regarding the Yatra," said sources, disclosing what lies at the heart of this proposed solution. "The rest — land transfer, its revocation and everything else — be treated as null and void."

As per Section 16 of the Shri Amarnath Shrine Board Act, the Board has the following roles and responsibilities:

• To undertake for the benefit of worshippers and pilgrims the construction of buildings for their accommodation (the Board had already been planning insulated huts with cushioned bunks keeping in view the fragile ecology of the region)

• Construction of sanitary works

• Improvement of means of communication

• Make provision of medical relief to pilgrims

• Arrange for proper worship at shrine

• Undertake developmental activity concerning the areas of the shrine and its surroundings

• Make arrangements for safe custody of funds, valuables and jewellery and preservation of Board funds

• Make provision for suitable emoluments to salaried staff

• Make suitable arrangements for imparting religious instructions and general education to pilgrims
