But he stressed that in the global rankings of major economies, "the long-term economic fundamentals of the United States compare very favorably."

The Treasury chief defended a government lifeline thrown to the mortgage finance giants Freddie Mac and Fannie Mae, which together account for about 70 per cent of all US home loans.

Plunging share values and shocking losses have raised new questions about the two firms' solvency, but Paulson said he had no plans to tap his new authority to buy equity in the companies to boost their capital. "Well, we have no plans to insert money in either of those institutions," he told NBC.

"I think it was very important that we get these temporary backup facilities, because Fannie and Freddie are important to our capital markets broadly," he said.

He said that following US economic growth of 1.9 per cent in the second quarter, which was better than the first quarter's 0.9 per cent pace, "my view would be let's see how this program works in the third quarter." Paulson, agreeing with Bush that Wall Street had got "drunk" and was now suffering a hangover, said new regulation was needed to cope with the daunting complexity of modern banking's investment practices.

Heading: New rate spreads for overseas borrowing - Indian Express
Content:
The high-level Chaturvedi Committee has recommended raising petrol prices by Rs 2.50 a litre per month till March 2009 and diesel prices by Rs 0.75 per litre till 2010 to eliminate subsidies on the two fuels.

The three-member panel, headed by Planning Commission member B K Chaturvedi that was asked by the Prime Minister to go into the financial position of oil firms, also suggested levying a "Metro Extra" tax of Rs 2 per litre on diesel, in four installments in large cities where the fuel was being used in expensive cars.

Sources said the committee, besides suggesting freeing auto fuel pricing from government control, also recommended changes in distribution of domestic LPG by restricting only six refills per connection a year.

Currently, Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum are compensated for losses on sale of petrol, diesel, domestic LPG and kerosene through a combination of government bonds and discounts from upstream firms such as ONGC.

The committee also suggested slashing import duty on petrol and diesel to zero (from 2.5 per cent) as has been done in the case of crude oil, domestic kerosene and LPG. Excise duty on petrol be reduced from Rs 13.75 per litre to Rs 10.

Sources said it also favoured imposing a new tax on oil produced from fields awarded prior to the advent of New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP) in 1999 — state-run firms such as ONGC would be stripped of any gains above $75 a barrel while private companies such as Cairn would be taxed at 40 per cent for gains over this benchmark rate.

The report is yet to be accepted by the government and it looks unlikely that with inflation rate crossing 12 per cent and general elections not far, suggestions will be accepted in toto. Doubts have already been expressed whether the report will be implemented, given the high rate of inflation and elections in less than a year's time.

Petroleum Minister Murli Deora had yesterday stated, "We are studying the report that the Chaturvedi Committee submitted, and it will be premature to presume that the suggestions made by the committee were being implemented.

Heading: Airport number two for Delhi unlikley - Indian Express
Content:
India will not raise limits for corporate foreign borrowing despite pressure from firms wanting to tap cheaper funds amid rising rates at home, but may revise interest rate spreads, a finance ministry official said. Smaller firms are finding it hard to raise cash to fund expansion after several rounds of tightening by the Reserve Bank of India.

Analysts say capital inflows have slowed enough to make a further relaxation in external commercial borrowing guidelines possible. But the official, who could not be identified, said the government saw no need to change the rules, while it could consider modifying interest rate spreads. "We have received several representations to revisit the spreads. We are looking into it," the official said.

Last year, the government tightened ECB regulations to reduce high capital inflows which were pushing up the rupee and complicating monetary management. But in May, it raised the proportion of overseas borrowing a company can bring into India.

Firms can now borrow up to $500 million a year, but manufacturers are only allowed to bring in to India $50 million and infrastructure companies $100 million. The rest must be invested in units overseas.

In the last two months, the central bank has raised its key lending rate by 125 basis points in three steps in a bit to rein in inflation at 13-year highs, pushing up credit costs. Indian firms currently borrow funds overseas at 200 basis points over Libor for a 3-5 year loan, and the spread is 350 basis points for loans above five years.

"Probably the thinking now is to slow domestic demand but the willingness to revisit the spreads is a positive development. Without it, smaller firms are facing problems to raise funds," said D.K. Joshi, principal economist at ratings and research agency Crisil.

India, Asia's third-largest economy is expected to expand by 8 per cent in 2008/09, lower than 9 per cent in the previous fiscal year.

$500 mn

The money firms are allowed to borrow from abroad under current rules

$50 mn

The money manufacturers are allowed to bring into the country

$100 mn

The money infrastructure companies allowed to get into the country

Heading: SC notice to PwC on advance tax - Indian Express
Content:
Even as congestion at Delhi airport worsens by the day, the chances of a second airport coming up in the national capital continue to remain slim, with a group of ministers (GoM) constituted in February still looking into legalities of approving a second airport in view of agreements signed with the developers of IGI airport.

At a meeting of the Consultative Committee of Members of Parliament attached to the civil aviation ministry, minister of civil aviation Praful Patel said that the GoM was reviewing the matter, as the government had "legal and contractual obligations" with the GMR-led consortium that is currently revamping the airport. The members also discussed other issues like the necessity of an airport at Jhajjar in Haryana, which is one of the states without any airport at present.

The minister also informed the committee that work on modernisation of Kolkata and Chennai airports would begin next month, soon after the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs clears these mega projects. The two airports, as per the recommendations of the respective state governments, would be developed by the state-owned AAI and not privatised.

Patel also said that trial runs on the new third runway of IGI Airport would begin in ten days. Once operational, it would ease the air traffic congestion over the Delhi airspace.

The minister also raised the issue of rising aviation turbine fuel prices affecting the profitability of Indian carriers. He said that the base price of ATF in India was high primarily due to subsidisation of other petroleum products, adding that the high taxes levied on jet fuel by state governments further compounded the problem.

Informing the committee that he had raised the issue with the PM , Patel said a panel headed by the cabinet secretary has been constituted to examine and assess the problems faced by the industry.

Heading: Agriculture ministry opposes ceiling on raw cotton export - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court today sought reply from PriceWaterhouseCoopers (PwC) as to why the non-resident company should not pay advance tax on fee charged by it for providing services in India.

A bench headed by Justice S H Kapadia issued notice to PwC, being a non-resident firm, on an appeal filed by the Income Tax department seeking the apex court's interference on the issue whether other statutory provisions charging interest can be applied to the assessee which had failed to pay advance tax. The department has challenged the sectoral tribunal's ruling which held that PwC was not liable to pay advance tax even if the entire payment made to it by its clients in India was subject to TDS. It had also sought the apex court's directions on whether an assessee like PwC whose entire taxable receipts were subject to TDS was liable to pay advance tax and if the same was paid then whether interest was chargeable on it.

PwC had disclosed consultancy fee aggregating to more than Rs 5.88 crore during 2001-02 arising from various services rendered to its clients in India. PwC, a limited liability partnership firm, had filed return declaring total income of Rs 5.88 crore on which the tax was worked out to be more than Rs 2.02 crore. In its computation of income filed along with income return, the assessee had adjusted the amount of TDS aggregating to more than Rs 1.47 crore and the shortfall of tax of Rs 66.64 lakh inclusive of interest was deposited under Section 140A.

Heading: NTPC responsible for its own plight : Coal Ministry - Indian Express
Content:
The Agriculture Ministry has opposed fixing of any quantitative ceiling on exports of raw cotton for the current year as it would adversely affect cotton-growers who have begun fetching reasonable returns due to rising domestic prices and export demands.

In a recent meeting the Committee of Secretaries (CoS) observed that the proposal of the Textiles Ministry on fixing a quantitative ceiling on exports of raw cotton for the current year up to September 30 was disfavoured by the Agriculture Ministry headed by Sharad Pawar as it feels that any further restrictions on exports on quick succession to the recent measures already taken like abolition of customs duty on import of raw cotton and removal of drawback benefits on exports of raw cotton would adversely affect cotton growers .

The prices of raw cotton are above the Minimum Support Price (MSP), but could be lowered than the MSP as it was referred for revisal to the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).

"Hence the issue needs to be examined again by the Agriculture Ministry keeping in view the current MSP and the likely revision in MSP for which it could also seek opinion of the Department of Economic Affairs," the CoS has reasoned.

Heading: Nahata threatens legal action against Dhoot - Indian Express
Content:
Holding the state-run thermal power giant NTPC squarely responsible for its plants facing critical and super-critical coal stock position, the Coal Ministry today lashed out at the PSU saying frequent breakdowns of its transportation coupled with reluctance to off take adequate coal has resulted in its current plight.

National Thermal Power Corporation's (NTPC) 43 plants face critical coal stock position implying that they have reserves less than 7 days while 23 of its plants are even facing super-critical position meaning that they have coal reserves of less than four days. The PSU is said to be battling with coal shortage of about 10-12 million tonne a year and is planning to import about 7 MT this fiscal to bridge the shortfall in the total requirement of 125 million tonne. The PSU's top brass have already apprised the top officials of the Power Ministry on the coal shortage, which has reportedly assumed alarming proportions. Unless Coal Ministry and its PSUs expedite their supply, it could result in closure of plants, it said.

"Last year we supplied 95 per cent coal to NTPC, and this year we have already assured 105 per cent of coal for meeting their production requirements. But they are unable to arrest their own ailments including frequent breakdowns of their Merry-Go-Round systems impacting their unloading capabilities," a senior Coal Ministry official told The Indian Express. Another factor affecting the power giant's operational efficacy is its failure to carry out routine maintenance works for better utilisation of calorific value of coal.

Moreover, their Plant Load Factor (PLF) has also shot up considerably high generating further demand of coal compelling CIL to shuffle its coal supply. Whenever any plant reports near depletion , the PSU has to rush the mineral from its nearest subsidiary to its rescue, the official said.

"We know that NTPC is supposed to import about 10 million tones of coal to meet its growing needs, which they have not done so far which amply explains that they are running on coal supplied by Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries, then where is the cause for complaint?" the official questioned. He pointed out that CIL is supplying coal to them at $30 a tonne while international coal prices are around $130 a tonne" and that is why perhaps NTPC is averse to importing coal, but if they averse to offtaking coal from their pitheads for the fear of rising inventories, then the Coal Ministry can do very little about it," the official said.

Heading: Submarine collision: found guilty, Navy Commander quits - Indian Express
Content:
About two months back Videocon chairman Venugopal Dhoot announced that Datacom would launch mobile services on August 15. Launch of services is no where in sight. However, the promoters of the company are set to land in the court with Mahendra Nahata threatening to take legal action against Dhoot. Datacom Solutions had earlier filed caveat against its original promoter Jumbo Techno Services Pvt Ltd (a company owned Mahendra Nahata's family).

The dispute between the two began when Jumbo raised issues related to corporate governance and shareholders agreement. Dhoot-owned Videocon is the largest shareholder in the company with 64 per cent shareholding, while Jumbo owns the rest 36 per cent. Later, the two began negotiations which focused on Dhoot buying Nahata's share at a price which was earlier agreed by the two partners in shareholders agreement.

Heading: Sweet tidings from Assam post office - Indian Express
Content:
The Commander of a Navy Submarine that was involved in an accident with a merchant ship in the Arabian Sea in January has quit the service after a Board of Inquiry held him responsible for the incident.

Naval Commander Narendra Kumar, who was the Commanding Officer of the Russian origin Kilo Class Submarine INS Sindhughosh when it brushed against a massive cargo ship during a routine exercise off the Gujarat coast, put in his papers last month.

Sources in the Navy said the officer, who was posted to administrative duties in Delhi after the incident, decided to quit the Navy rather than face a Court Martial where he was set to be dismissed from service.

The Board of Inquiry, which was set up immediately after the incident, concluded that as Commander of the submarine, Kumar could not escape responsibility for the accident that caused damage to the fins, periscope and aerials of the naval vessel. Sources indicated that the second in command of the submarine would also put in his papers, taking responsibility for the failure.

A major tragedy was averted on January 17 when one of the most advanced submarines of the Navy collided with a foreign merchant ship, MV Leeds, in the Arabian sea during a training exercise.

The diesel powered submarine brushed aside the massive cargo ship as it was trying to surface in shallow waters during the Western Fleet war games. All 53 crew members on board escaped unhurt but the submarine suffered damaged and will remain out of service for several months.

As it was taking part in a simulated wargame where it had to evade the 'enemy' in 'restricted waters', the submarine had switched off sonar and its radar was not transmitting any signals. While the vessel performed a periscope scan before proceeding to surface, its commander failed to detect the merchant ship.

"The submarine was operating at a precarious depth and could not dive to escape due to the restricted waters," a Navy officer had then said. The merchant ship, that wasn't damaged in the incident, was not found at fault as it was operating as per the rules of the sea.

Scare on the high seas

• 2005: Speeding stealth frigate INS Trishul got extensively damaged after a collision with a merchant vessel off the Mumbai coast

•April 2006: INS Prahar sunk off the Goa coast after colliding with merchant ship MV Rajiv Gandhi.

•September 2006: Guided missile frigate INS Dunagiri had a close shave after it struck a glancing blow with a Shipping Corporation of India merchant vessel off the Mumbai coast

Heading: Army insensitive to religious sentiments: Meghalaya devotees - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian postal services may no longer be preferred by the urban population, but for rural Assam it could well prove to be the platform that would give them their own brand name.

The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) initiative with India Post in Assam has decided to use the postal department's nationwide network to promote produce manufactured by the rural population of the state.

The new display-cum- sale counter opened on Monday at Meghdoot Bhavan — the Guwahati general post office (GPO) — in fact has a wide range of products from rural Assam, mostly produced by self-help groups and village cooperatives, with NABARD playing the match-maker's role between the postal department and the rural groups.

Over 250 bee-keepers under Dimoriya Grameen Vikash Samiti (DGVS)have produced about 2.5 tons of honey this season and are selling their produce through the good old post office.

"Our honey is being put on display in the Guwahati GPO from today for people to buy. And if everything goes well, Dimoriya honey might soon become available across the country through the network that the postal department has," said Mahendra Das the president of DGVS. Their target for next year is to produce at least 4 tones of honey.

"Since we have been supporting rural people in diversifying their economic activities to increase their income, it is also our responsibility to provide them the vital marketing link," said Ibrahim Padbidri, assistant general manager at the NABARD regional office. NABARD has already roped in six self-help groups and some other rural farmers groups like the one from Dimoriya.

"We are putting up plates and bowls made of dhokuwa (lower portion of betel-nut leaves) which can become an alternative to plastic and thermocol in marriage parties and other social gatherings," said Binita Kalita of Dhriti, an NGO based at Barpeta that supports 60 families earning a living from dhokuwa - previously considered as a waste product.

"We have already received bulk orders from Kolkata for dhokuwa plates and bowls especially during the durga puja season," she said.

Organic tamarind powder, pickles, khadi shoulder bags and endi shawls produced by tribal villagers in Karbi Anglong district have also found a new marketing outlet in the Guwahati GPO. "We have 50 women producing these items, and most of them are Karbi tribals," said Anish Nandy of Vivekananda Kendra at Khatkhati in Karbi Anglong.

The Business Development and Marketing Cell of India Post in Guwahati has already sold over 5,000 kgs of Assam tea across the country through the new initiative launched about two years ago. "Assam tea has found new buyers through the post office network in states like Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat and Bihar," said Monojit Kumar, chief postmaster general, Assam.

"We are also planning to open a sale counter at Kaziranga post office soon, so that foreign tourists are also attracted to these village products," added Pallab Hazarika, senior manager in the business development cell.

Heading: Manipur demands Kalmadi’s ouster over Monika row - Indian Express
Content: Devotees of Lord Shiva here are crying foul after the Army stopped them from using the cantonment area to reach the Shiva temple in Madhavkhola, one of the oldest Shiva temples in Shillong. The Army has constructed a gate and posted guards in the cantonment to prevent people from using the area as a shortcut to reach the temple on a hillock. Raj Kanwar, a devotee, said: "How can elderly people and children take the long highway to the temple? We have been using the shortcut for almost 50 years now. Why has the Army turned insensitive to religious sentiment of the devotees."   The Defence PRO Wing Commander Rajeev Sisodia, however, defended the Army's decision to close the shortcut and cited security reasons behind it.

Heading: Meghalaya to introduce work permits for migrants - Indian Express
Content:
The Manipur Government on Monday sent a formal request to the Centre seeking a CBI probe into Laishram Monika Devi's doping charges. State Chief Secretary, Rakesh, wrote a letter to Union Secretary Satyananda Mishra, Ministry of Personnel and Public Grievances, and formally sought a CBI probe into the role of the Indian Olympic Association(IOA) and Sports Authority of India(SAI).

Meanwhile the Coordinating Committee Against Monika's Withdrawal from Beijing Olympics, assembled at the Manipur Olympic Association office at Imphal on Monday demanding an apology from the Centre for the fiasco. Many organisations have decided to take necessary legal actions against SAI and demanded removal of Suresh Kalmadi from the post of the president of the IOA.

Heading: ULFA strike on I-Day, night trains cancelled - Indian Express
Content:
Learning a lesson from Assam's migrant problem, the Meghalaya Government is trying to put in place a mechanism to stop the influx of Bangaldeshis as well as labourers from other parts of the country by introducing work permits for migrants.

The proposal of work permits for migrant labourers is a part of the Meghalaya Progressive Alliance (MPA) Government's Common Minimum Programme (CMP).

Meghalaya Chief Minister Donkupar Roy told reporters on Monday that the Government is examining the report submitted by the Cabinet Committee on Influx (CCI).

Chairman of the committee and Urban Affairs Minister Paul Lyngdoh has suggested in the report that the existing Inter-State Workmen Regulation Act, 1979, be tightened and made more effective. The report also suggests mandatory registration of contractors who hire labourers with the District Council and issuance of work permits to them.

The committee wants the work permits to be renewed every 179 days, so that the migrant labourers do not claim the right of permanent residency. As per the existing laws, any Indian citizen who resides at place for over six months may apply for permanent residency.

The Khasi Students Union (KSU), which had earlier spearheaded many agitations against Bangladeshi migrants, is putting pressure on the state Government to immediately implement the CCI recommendations of introducing the work permit. The students body has threatened to launch an agitation if the Government fails to introduce the work permit for migrant labourers soon.

Former Lok Sabha speaker and Meghalaya Planning Board chairman Purno A Sangma said that Meghalaya must learn a lesson from Assam and Tripura, where Bangladeshi nationals have infiltrated and changed the demography of the two states.

Heading: Pro-migrant group calls bandh in Assam today - Indian Express
Content:
Night running of trains has been cancelled across Assam for five days beginning tomorrow in view of the outlawed United Liberation Front of Assam (ULFA) and three other outfits of the region calling a general strike on Independence Day. Intelligence agencies have also sent an alert about jehadi elements trying to strike in the run-up to August 15.

A spokesman of the Northeast Frontier Railways here said all trains from Dibrugarh and Guwahati bound for destinations elsewhere in the country would now start during the daytime instead of night.

Other three outfits apart from the ULFA that have given a call for strike and boycott during Independence Day are Kamatapur Liberation Organisation (KLO), Manipur People's Liberation Front (MPLF) and Tripura People's Democratic Front (TPDF).

The four groups have issued a joint statement asking people to boycott Independence Day in view of "India's occupation of the Northeastern region".

Heading: Saxena, carrier of cash, vanishes from scene - Indian Express
Content:
The All Assam Minority Students' Union (AAMSU), a pro-migrant group, has called a 12-hour bandh in the state on Tuesday to protest alleged harassment of minorities in the name of detecting the migrants.

The AAMSU alleges that various groups in the state, especially the All Assam Students' Union (AASU), have been harassing Muslims in different districts claiming them to be Bangladeshi infiltrators.

The AASU has, however, hit back, saying it was only demanding expulsion of Bangladeshi migrants in keeping with the law.

Heading: Sardesai appears before parliamentary panel - Indian Express
Content:
The CNN-IBN telecast of the "cash-for-votes" sting operation on Monday turned the spotlight on Sanjeev Saxena and Sohail Hindustani who figured in the tapes.

While not much is known about Hindustani, the BJP has been working overtime to provide "linkages" between Saxena and Amar Singh. In their July 24 letter to the Lok Sabha Speaker, the BJP had thrown hints of Saxena's links with Amar Singh. Now, the party says they had subsequently handed over much more "evidence" on him to the parliamentary panel.

The evidence the BJP has collected includes call detail records (CDRs) of Saxena's mobile phone, which incidentally, is registered with the HFCL company.

The CDRs, available with The Indian Express, reveal that several calls were made from the telephone on July 22 to Amar Singh's residence. The BJP has claimed Saxena was making these calls from 4 Ferozeshah Road, the residence of Ashok Argal where the cash was delivered to the BJP MPs. A number of other calls were made to mobile phones of other aides and secretaries of Amar Singh and a few to Saxena's own residence.

The BJP has also alleged that the white Gypsy in which Saxena arrived at 4 Ferozeshah Road provides a useful Amar Singh link, since the vehicle belongs to Pankaja Arts and Credit, a company in which Amar Singh's wife has a stake. The BJP has also claimed that Saxena's son had submitted the address of Amar Singh's official residence as his own for his college admission.

To political journalists in the capital, Saxena has been one of the assistants who used to send SMSes to journalists informing about Amar Singh's press conferences. In fact, he had sent his last SMS on July 20, before the special session of the Lok Sabha called for the trust vote.

Since the "cash-for-votes" scam surfaced in the Lok Sabha on July 22, his mobile phone has been "temporarily out of service".

Saxena, who is seen delivering the cash to the BJP MPs, lived in house number 186 of Ramakrishna Apartments in East Delhi's IP Extension.

In fact, four days after the trust vote, Saxena's home was found locked when The Indian Express team went there. His neighbours said the Saxena family had not been spotted after the trust vote.

Heading: Personnel dept asked to look into charges of CBI seeking BSP votes - Indian Express
Content:
After the deposition of CNN-IBN television channel editor-in-chief Rajdeep Sardesai, the special Lok Sabha committee headed by V Kishore Chandra Deo here on Monday moved ahead and sent summons to some key players for August 18 in the cash-for-votes scam.

Those listed for recording evidence next, according to Deo, are Samajwadi Party MP Reoti Raman Singh, Sudheendra Kulkarni, a former aide of BJP leader L K Advani, Sanjeev Saxena, a supposed aide of SP general secretary Amar Singh, and Raja Hindustani, a former BJP Yuva Morcha activist.

Sources said Sardesai told members in reply to questions that it might have been the presumption of BJP members, but he had made no promise to telecast the sting operation on July 22 as claimed by them. He said once BJP members Ashok Argal, Faggan Singh Kulaste and Mahavir Bhagora had brought bundles of currency notes amounting to Rs 1 crore into the House, he had decided not to telecast the operation. Sardesai, according to sources, maintained that the channel, in accordance with its own code of ethics, felt called upon to speak to other people too whose names figured in the episode.

He said the channel found it necessary to tie some loose ends.

CNN-IBN, Sardesai maintained, had the right to telecast the operation. He handed over two more tapes, one visual and the other audio, to the committee along with a full transcript.

He denied the charge that the tapes had been doctored. The tapes are likely to be circulated among the members on Tuesday.

The names of Reoti Raman Singh and Saxena figured in the complaint of BJP MPs. Reoti Raman, they had claimed, had approached them first. Reoti Raman represents the Allahabad Lok Sabha constituency. He had defeated senior BJP leader Murli Manohar Joshi. Saxena, according to the complainants, had delivered the slush money to them.

When asked why the committee had sent for Kulkarni, Deo told The Indian Express, "We felt it necessary to call him." Kulkarni has claimed being a witness to the alleged bribery in his writings since. Sources in the committee said looking at the recording, Kulkarni seems to be among those who masterminded the operation.

Deo said the committee would try to record Bhagora's evidence, depending upon his health condition. Bhagora has not been able to do so due to a heart ailment.

Heading: PM should come clean on allegations: BJP - Indian Express
Content:
Even as a House panel is looking into the cash-for-votes scam, the Lok Sabha Secretariat is learnt to have requested the Personnel and Home departments to look into allegations of a CBI officer coercing BSP MPs to support the UPA Government in the July 22 trust vote.

Sources said the move comes after BSP general secretary S C Mishra requested Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee to look into the matter.

During the discussion on the trust vote in Parliament, BSP MP Brajesh Pathak had alleged that a CBI officer contacted him at his residence and mounted pressure on him to support the UPA Government. The CBI officer in return offered to adopt leniency in the DA case pending against BSP chief Mayawati, Pathak had further alleged.

Pathak along with his party MPs had even flashed a copy of documents given to him by the officer in the Lok Sabha that day. Subsequently, Pathak also lodged a complaint with the Lok Sabha Speaker on July 22, seeking an inquiry into the incident.

While the BSP wanted the incident to be probed by the privilege committee of Lok Sabha, its complaint lost out to the 'cash-for-vote' scam. It was only after S C Mishra's request that the Lok Sabha Secretariat requested the Department of Personnel, under which the CBI falls, to look into the incident.

With the BSP now pressing for an inquiry into the alleged threat by a government functionary, it appears that the party is bracing for another showdown with the Congress-led Government after Mayawati's attempt to mobilise support against the Government in the trust vote.

The move also holds significance in view of the fact that the court had postponed the hearing on the DA case to November this year. The BSP may now press for the completion of inquiry ahead of the hearing or seek its postponement.

Heading: New Bihar PCC chief - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP on Monday has asked Prime Minister Manmohan Singh "to respond to the allegations faced by some of his ministerial colleagues".

"The Prime Minister must come clean on some his ministerial colleagues facing allegations," said party spokesperson Rajiv Pratap Rudy. The BJP MP said "investigations by a news channel found that Union Railway Minister Lalu Prasad was using his position to accumulate wealth."

He also said SP chief "Mulayam Singh Yadav had supported the lifting of ban on SIMI" and "UPA ally PDP is supporting attempts to take trucks from Jammu and Kashmir to Muzaffarabad violating the country's laws".

Heading: Maharashtra Cong crisis to be over in two days: Alva - Indian Express
Content: Anil Kumar Sharma, former Patna University Students Union president, was on Monday appointed new PCC president of Bihar replacing Sadanand Singh. Senior leader Vijay Shankar Dubey was made the chairman of the state Congress Campaign Committee. Five working presidents have also been appointed to assist Sharma. The Campaign Committee will have four convenors and a spokesperson along with more than 60 members. The list has several members from the upper castes, including Sharma, clearly indicating the Congress' plan to woo upper castes when the backward castes are divided among the JD(U), the RJD, and others.

Heading: Govt should put an end to persistent deprivation of human lives: Amartya Sen - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and Revenue Minister Narayan Rane rushed to Delhi to meet Congress chief Sonia Gandhi over the latter's resignation drama, the AICC in-charge of party affairs in Maharashtra Margaret Alva on Monday said the issues of Rane's resignation and the appointment of a successor to Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee (MPCC) chief Prabha Rau would be settled within two days.

Speaking to reporters after a function to felicitate Rau on her being appointed as the Governor of Himachal Pradesh, Alva said Sonia would take a decision on Rane's resignation. "I can't comment on this issue, only Soniaji will take a decision," she said, adding that she would return to New Delhi immediately to discuss the pending issues with the party high command.

Commenting on the Videocon deal, over which Rane had thrown tantrums in the Cabinet meeting last week and had opted to step down as a minister, she said, "It was a collective decision of the cabinet and not of an individual." Rane had objected to the deal on grounds that Deshmukh had bulldozed the decision to grant a prime plot of land to the company near the proposed airport in Navi Mumbai at a throwaway price. After the Cabinet meeting on August 5, Rane addressed public meetings at various places in the state, criticising Deshmukh of favouring industrialists at the cost of the common man.

When contacted, Rane said, "I have full faith in Madam (Sonia). I am sure that she knows what I have done is in the interest of the people and the party. I will go by her decision." He, however, clarified he was not contemplating leaving the party as of now.

"The Congress President knows everything. She knows what is in public interest and what is not. Whenever she calls me, I will go and explain everything. I will take a decision (about future course) only after that. I will not quit the party, but I will not be a minister. While staying in the party, I will see how Vilasrao Deshmukh does his best to bring the Shiv Sena-BJP back to power in Maharashtra," said Rane.

Earlier, he had shot off two letters to the Congress President — one exposing the functioning and non-performance of the Deshmukh Government and the other being a copy of the resignation letter addressed to the Governor. He was, however, silent on whether he had sent the said resignation to the Governor.

Asked about the party's displeasure on his public outbursts, Rane told The Indian Express: "I cannot keep my mouth shut if somebody compromises on public interest. Deshmukh is busy serving his own interests. I will not work under his leadership."

Heading: Soren eye fixed on his chair, Koda digs heels in - Indian Express
Content:
As the country's political elite sat all ears, Noble Laureate Amartya Sen here on Monday made a passionate plea for an immediate removal of long-standing deprivations of disadvantaged people. He was delivering the inaugural Hiren Mukherjee Memorial lecture at the Central Hall of Parliament.

The august gathering included Vice-President Mohammad Hamid Ansari, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee, Congress president Sonia Gandhi and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha L K Advani.

Sen said it was true that the Government had to respond to "ongoing priorities," but it must address "gigantic older problems of persistent deprivation of human lives, tolerated without much political protest". "Justice demands that we make a strong effort to identify the overwhelming priorities that have to be confronted with total urgency. We have to ask what should keep us awake at night."

The Prime Minister, who warmly hugged his "friend" Sen at the function, acknowledged that the "policies and principles of our Government, as indeed the intellectual inspiration for the National Common Minimum Programme, are drawn from the world view that Amartya Sen has come to represent". "This world view is captured by what our Government has defined as inclusive growth," Singh said.

Having accepted Sen's inspirational role vis-à-vis his Government's policies, the Prime Minister moved over to pack his speech with political punch. With some leading lights from the CPI(M) like Sitaram Yechury and Basudeb Acharia seated in the front row, the Prime Minister showered praise on Somnath Chatterjee.

"We are also privileged that this lecture is being delivered in the presence of a true inheritor of the legacy of Hiren Mukherjee (CPI-M leader), our distinguished speaker, Shri Somnath Chatterjee," he said.

Singh then concluded his speech with the remarks: "I would also like to take this opportunity to pay tribute to the inspirational leadership of our distinguished Speaker. The entire country has come to look up to him for balance and fair play in the functioning of the Lok Sabha."

Sen listed child undernourishment, lack of medical attention for the poor and absence of basic schooling for large sections of the society as "momentous manifestations of severe injustice" in India.

"Whatever else nyaya may demand, the reasoned humanity of nyaya can hardly fail to demand the urgent removal of these terrible deprivations of human lives," he said. Dwelling on the difference between the Sanskrit terms niti and nyaya — both meaning justice — he said nyaya stands for actual social realisations, going beyond organisations and rules. He said "nyaya is not just a matter of judging institutions and rules, but of judging societies." He made a forceful contention for the prevention of what he called matsyanyaya, in which the big fish freely devours the small fish.

Heading: Paswan to take war against Maya to her doorstep - Indian Express
Content:
With the Congress not keen and RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav firmly opposed to Shibu Soren as Chief Minister of Jharkahand, the JMM chief, in a last-ditch effort, is learnt to have threatened to withdraw support and topple the state's Madhu Koda Government.

While Soren and some of his party MPs continue to camp in New Delhi and hound the Congress leadership with the demand for Jharkhand's top post, the JMM has called a meeting in Ranchi on August 17 to decide its future course of action. That they were in a fix was understandable as JMM MPs refused to talk to the media and Soren as usual was "untraceable".

Sources close to the JMM chief, however, said that they have already told the Koda Government that they will withdraw support if the UPA continues to "dilly-dally" over their demand to install Shibu Soren as chief minister.The JMM, with 17 MLAs in the 82-member Jharkhand Assembly, happens to be the largest UPA constituent in the state, and if it pulls out, the Koda government would be reduced to a minority.

Unperturbed by the threat, Jharkhand Chief Minister Madhu Koda reached here and ruled out any threat to his leadership. Contrary to his earlier willingness to quit and make way for Soren if the UPA so wanted, Koda on Monday clearly indicated that he would stay put. "I will be leading the UPA in Jharkahand. I enjoy the full trust of the UPA leaders," said an exuberant Koda.

Sources said that behind Koda's confidence was RJD boss Lalu Yadav who was firmly backing him and even weighing upon the Congress leadership to refrain from any change of guard in the state. Koda suits both Lalu as well as the Congress as he is easily pliable while Soren is known for acting independently.

His threat to withdraw support notwithstanding, analysts feel that Soren's political compulsions leave with him almost no option but to remain with the UPA. Referring to criminal cases pending against him, they argue that Guruji (Soren) cannot afford to withdraw and face the CBI. Moreover, now the NDA too would not be interested in projecting him for the top post in the state.

Heading: Maya can’t become PM by winning UP alone: Cong - Indian Express
Content:
Dalit leader and LJP chief Ramvilas Paswan has decided to take on arch rival BSP supremo Mayawati in her own turf. Paswan declared on Monday that his party team would visit Mayawati's native village Badalpur and launch an agitation against "forced" capture of poor farmers' land.

"This is more dangerous than Nandigram. Mayawati is capturing poor farmers' land to build a house, garden on the roof and helipad for her personal use. We cannot be mute spectators. Our party will launch an agitation against this and ensure that the farmers get back their land," an angry Paswan told reporters. He said that in West Bengal, the Government was acquiring land in Nandigram for setting up an industry but here, she was doing so for her personal use. "This is a crime," he said.

Paswan is known for his animosity towards "dalit icon" and UP Chief Minister Mayawati. Though Paswan primarily derives his political strength from Bihar, he has been focusing on UP these days to take on his dalit rival. He has visited the state a number of times recently and held party rallies.

Though averse to joining hands with RJD chief Lalu Yadav in Bihar, Paswan is learnt to be keen on a tie-up with the SP-Congress combine in UP to lend his support in weakening Mayawati in the state.

Reacting strongly to Mayawati's heir announcement at her Lucknow rally, Paswan charged that she was treating UP as her personal property. "She is installing her own statues. Then she is declaring her heir. Is UP a temple or monastery or her personal property that she is declaring a heir," Paswan asked and charged Mayawati of being an opportunist leader who had nothing to do with the welfare of dalits.

Heading: Chhattisgarh CM poll plan: a quiz on state - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress on Monday accused Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati of "emotionally blackmailing" the people by talking of a threat to her life and her "political heir".

Addressing a press conference, AICC general secretary and UP in-charge Digvijay Singh said apprehensions of a threat to Mayawati's life was the handiwork of a coterie of bureaucrats around her.

"These officials have terrorised Mayawati so as to prevent her from meeting the common people and getting first-hand information about the corrupt practices of the bureaucrats," he said.

Taking strong exception of Mayawati's allegation that the Congress was trying to eliminate her, Singh said she should give proof to support her allegation. "The Congress subscribes to the ideology of harmony and non-violence. If Mayawati feels so insecure, then the UPA Government at the Centre can provide more NSG commandos for her security," he added.

The AICC general secretary said that Mayawati, by announcing that her political heir would be from her own sub-caste, had shattered the unity of Dalit community and this was also against the ideals of Dr B R Ambedkar and BSP founder Kanshi Ram.

Rebutting the charge that the Congress was against Mayawati becoming the Prime Minister, Singh said, "The Congress will have no objection if Mayawati becomes the Prime Minister, but a simple fact is that even if she wins all the 80 Lok Sabha seats in UP, her dream will not be fulfilled till the entire country supports her."

Commenting on the Badalpur land row, he asked Mayawati to clarify how her father could purchase land in the area after a notification of land acquisition was issued. "The Congress will continue to agitate against the wrong-doings of the BSP Government at Badalpur even if the party leaders are arrested under the National Security Act (NSA)," he said.

The AICC leader said talks with the Samajwadi Party for a pre-poll alliance were underway. "The Congress always supports unity of the secular forces in the country and the SP has the distinction to prevent the BJP in the state," he said.

Singh also said his party had no objection if the SP joined the Centre, but the decision has to be taken by the leadership of both the parties and the Prime Minister.

When asked about the possibility of Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) joining their alliance, he said the doors were open for Ajit Singh, "but the RLD chief is a fickle-minded person that is why he is in trouble".

Heading: After a lull, monsoon set to pick up over central, western India - Indian Express
Content:
Ahead of the Assembly polls, Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Dr Raman Singh has come up with an innovative idea: a quiz contest for the masses. Titled "Hamar Chhattisgarh", the quiz contest, organised to mark India's 61st Independence Day, will have 61 questions pertaining to the state, which was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in November 2000.

The questionnaire for this block-level quiz contest has been published in local newspapers and participants will have to fill it up and send it to the State Public Relations Department before August 14. Ten contestants from each of the 146 blocks, who give correct answers to all the questions, would get a cash award of Rs 1,000 each. However, the winners would be selected through lottery if more than 10 participants in any block correctly answered all questions.

Participants giving more than 60 per cent correct answers would get a certificate, signed by Chief Minister Raman Singh himself, besides attractive prizes.

Heading: Villagers brave waters to go to work - Indian Express
Content:
After playing flip-flop for most of the season, the monsoon is finally showing signs getting back to normal. Good rains are expected in the next 3-5 days in central and western parts of the country which have received deficient rainfall till now.

A well-marked, low-pressure area is developing over Orissa and its adjoining areas, and there are also indications of a mid-tropospheric circulation of wind building up over Gujarat and Konkan region.

Coupled together, these two wind systems are likely to result in a good amount of rainfall in most parts of central and western India, a weather scientist said.

Most of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Konkan and Goa, Saurashtra, Chhattisgarh, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Telengana have received poor rainfall this season. Kerala, Lakshadweep and the Northeast have also had very less rainfall.

The formation of the complementary wind systems over Orissa and Gujarat is a welcome sign and it is very likely to result in rains in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Saurashtra and Gujarat, said the weather scientist.

However, this is not likely to benefit the southern-most parts of the country —Kerala and Lakshadweep — which will have to await the formation of offshore troughs and vortices along the western coast of India.

There are also signs that the monsoon winds have picked in strength, which is another welcome development, he said.

The monsoon, after a dramatic onset, has shown a highly deviant behaviour. For the first five weeks after the rains began, it poured in excess in most of the northern and eastern parts of the country.

But then followed a period of lull for about two weeks. The monsoon revived in the last week of July, this time bringing good rains to south India, barring Kerala and Lakshadweep, and some parts of central India, Maharashtra and Karnataka. During this time, the northern and eastern parts received below normal rainfall.

For most part, the monsoon winds have been weaker in strength because of which the formation of offshore troughs and vortices along the west coast has not happened.

This has resulted in below-normal rainfall in Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Konkan and Saurashtra region.

The weaker strength is also the reason why few low-pressure areas have been formed.

According to the weather scientist, as against its normal northwards speed of 100km per day, the monsoon winds advanced at almost double the speed this year, reaching Delhi about two weeks before its normal date and spreading over the entire country at least five days in advance.

As a result, when it should have been raining in the south, the monsoon had already advanced and reached the northernmost parts of the country.

By August 6, rainfall all over the country had only been one per cent below the normal, but there were wide regional variations. Northwestern India received excess rainfall, while in Central, South and northeastern parts the rainfall was below the long-period average (LPA) over the corresponding time.

Nineteen out of 36 meteorological sub-divisions had received rainfall less than their LPAs, seven of which were classified as deficient (20 to 60 per cent less than LPA).

Heading: Golden opportunity: Bindra Sr always had the eye for it - Indian Express
Content: Since the rains began, villagers of Maval taluka, about 50 km from Pune, have been wading through half a kilometre of swirling, chest-high waters to reach Kamshet, the nearest town, to meet daily needs or carry on their work. With the river Indrayani in spate, nearly 6,000 people of 25 villages in the taluka have been cut off from Kamshet. If they don't wade through the river, they will have to travel 60 km to reach the next nearest town, Talegaon. Police sub-inspector Balkrishna Sawant at Kamshet village said they had been appealing to the public not to take such risks, but they were not heeding the warning.

Heading: Any formula that helps give a feeling of confidence to people welcome: Governor - Indian Express
Content:
Trust Dr A S Bindra. He recognised an opportunity where others could see none.

Bindra prompted and encouraged his son Abhinav to take on shooting as a full time sport at a time when it had a limited following in India. Today he is "elated beyond words". He had extended him all the necessary support by providing him with a personal shooting range and arranging for foreign coaching in the initial years.

"Abhinav picked up the sport when he was only 12 and at that time no one knew shooting in India. We sent him to Germany for training. Then I got him a personal shooting range here in Chandigarh. I am extremely happy that he has made the country and his parents proud today," he said.

In fact, his acumen to identify gold displays itself in his business too. As the owner of Hi Tech Industries, a food processing and agri commodity firm based in Chandigarh, he identified a 'golden' opportunity in muck! He exports vermicompost — earthworm excreta — to various European nations. "Vermicompost is incredibly rich in humus. Earthworms eat cow dung or farm yard manure along with other wastes and pass it through their body. This process converts soil and manure to vermicompost. It has great value as an organic fertiliser," says Dr Bindra.

"In the developed world there is a lot of concern about finding an environmentally friendly way of getting rid of refuse. Earthworms are helpful in converting municipal waste, non-toxic solids, and household garbage into vermicompost. They not only convert garbage to manure, but also keep the environment healthy," says Bindra.

He also runs Bindra Agro Industires Corporation Limited, which makes ready-to-eat food and packed curries. Earlier he used to supply "Meals Ready to Eat" (MRE) packets to countries in Africa, Europe, Australia and to UN forces deputed at various locations including the peacekeeping mission in Sierra Leone.

"We have supplied food packets to the Indian Army also. There are lots of advantages about supplying food to the Army. Once you make a name for standard products many more buyers place their orders with you. Secondly, the Army is a bulk buyer. Certainly the Army demand has helped us in increasing our civilian orders too. As a company we have always tried to set the best standards in outsourcing and food processing," said Bindra.

Heading: No solution in sight, all-party meet hopes to keep eye on larger picture - Indian Express
Content:
In a telephonic interview with Ritu Sarin, Jammu and Kashmir Governor N N Vohra appeared cautious but admitted the past 40 days had been a "difficult" period for him as well as the beleaguered residents of the state. Excerpts:

Did the visit of the all-party delegation at all help in breaking the deadlock over the Amarnath land transfer issue?

That was a political move and the delegation was headed by Home Minister Shivraj Patil. He addressed the media in Srinagar and Jammu. I would not like to comment on the outcome of the visit.

But what I would like to say is that we have passed though difficult 40 days and are working intensively on a unanimous solution which is bound to emerge.

You have been closely associated with J&K in various capacities earlier. Has being appointed Governor at this stage been like a baptism of fire?

What you must remember is that despite all the disturbances and protest, the yatra is continuing without break. The politics has not disrupted the yatra per se. Of course, the number of yatris has come down drastically. The yatra to the Vaishno Devi shrine has also been affected. The number of tourists has fallen drastically and put together, this is a serious loss to the entire Jammu and Kashmir.

How do you react to the march of the fruit growers to Pak-occupied Kashmir?

Certain decisions were taken on Sunday night and all I can say is that the rule of law must prevail at any cost.

One formula presented by the BJP after the all-party meet is for the Amarnath Shrine Board Act to be adhered to again. What is your view?

I cannot say that I support the formula put forth by any political party. We are willing to look at any formulation which anyone can come up with which will help instill a feeling of confidence in the people of the state. This controversy has already had a big impact on the economy of the state and the sooner it ends the better.

What other confidence-building measures are you proposing?

S S Billoria, a former chief secretary, is being sent to Jammu to hold talks with members of the Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti. He has been nominated as a member of the new Board and though they have once turned the offer down, we want the Samiti to suggest some names of eminent people who can be on the Board. I hope they will agree this time. I also want members of the Samiti to visit the base camp at Amarnath. They should see what is happening on the ground for themselves. Also, I have proposed that a member of the Malik family (a Muslim shepherd by the name of Buta Malik is believed to have discovered the cave in 1850 AD) also be on the reconstituted Board.

In a TV interview given last week, you had said you were willing to step down as chairman of the Board to defuse the crisis. Are you still contemplating that step?

I want the economic hardships of the people to end. It has been a very bad time. For weeks, shops and commercial establishments have been shut and traffic disrupted. The estimated loss to the state is to the tune of Rs 2,000-3,000 crore. So I will consider the option of stepping down from chairmanship of the Board as the final step. For that, the law may also have to be changed.

Heading: All along route, Valley turns out for rally - Indian Express
Content:
With hardliners in the Valley, especially the Hurriyat Conference, gaining from the Amarnath row, different political parties on Monday looked willing to sink their differences to find an amicable solution to the crisis.

The all-party delegation, which had made a two-day visit to Jammu and Srinagar, met here on Monday but could not conclude its report as members of the delegation had to go for the Hiren Mukherjee memorial lecture by Nobel Laureate Amartya Sen in the Central Hall of Parliament. They will meet here again on Tuesday to deliberate over the possible ways to resolve the crisis and submit their report to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Wednesday.

In another positive development, the Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti (SASS) said that if the Centre sent it a peace proposal in writing, their legal committee would study it and decide whether to accept it or not. One of the solutions being worked out is adherence to the Shri Amarnath Shrine Board Act and the court interpretations of it, outlining the powers and functions of the Board.

SASS also warned the Centre to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Samiti leaders Leela Karan Sharma, Brig (Retd) Suchet Singh and Tilak Raj Sharma said the agitation will be intensified if this did not happen, including a "jail bharo aandolan" from August 18.

That Delhi is worried about any such escalation was evident at today's all-party meeting in the Capital. While there were differences of opinion over what led to the current crisis — with respective parties reiterating their familiar stances — there was reportedly a positive intent on the part of all, even though are were no concrete plans or proposals on the table as yet.

Union Ministers Raghuvansh Prasad, Saifuddin Soz and Prithviraj Chavan, former state CMs Farooq Abdullah and Ghulam Nabi Azad, Amar Singh and Sitaram Yechury were among those present at today's meeting.

"After rounds of allegations and counter-allegations, all parties, including the BJP, now look serious about a positive discussion on the way out of the present imbroglio," said a member of the delegation.

Representatives of all political parties were unanimous that a solution, acceptable to people from both Jammu and Kashmir, had to be worked out as hardliners in the Valley were trying to exploit the situation. Appreciating the "constructive" approach taken by the BJP's representative Arun Jaitley at today's meeting, a UPA delegate said there was unanimity that "pro-India mainstream parties in the Valley have to play a role so that the Hurriyat does not take the advantage in the Valley".

Ruling party sources said there were several "ideas" — but no concrete proposals — floating around. One of them was to hand over the contentious land to the state Tourism Department, which could make pre-fabricated structures for the duration of two months to provide facilities to visiting pilgrims and then dismantle those structures after it was over. Another idea was to seek the intervention of the Supreme Court of India.

Meanwhile, Union Minister and Jammu & Kashmir Congress chief Saifuddin Soz condemned the "most unfortunate" police firing at Sopore in Kashmir today. He talked to Governor N N Vohra to express concern. Home Minister Shivraj Patil also spoke to the Governor.

Heading: BJP is putting itself before nation: Cong - Indian Express
Content:
Beenish was only a little taller than the steel bucket she stood behind, on the right side of the road near Khawaja Bagh, Baramulla. As thousands of feet marched by on the highway from Srinagar, the six-year-old held out a half-filled tumbler of water, offering it to the processionists on their 'March to Muzaffarabad'.

As the marchers hit the road today, the villagers along the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad turned out in full strength. Those not participating, like the children, women and elderly, played host, offering water, juice, biscuits, bread and food to the protestors. People sat on the roadside to eat and take rest.

As Baramulla town got flooded with people around mid-day, announcements were made from the mosque loudspeakers: "Whatever food you have in your homes, bring it out on the road. We have to serve our guests." People obliged, women especially. "Why shouldn't I give them food, they are my children," said an elderly Khateeja.

As news came of security forces firing on protestors at Chahal, followed by motorcycles, cars and ambulances carrying the injured, people quickly started working out arrangements to host the protestors for the night.

All along the march route, the scenes were similar. The administration's measure of arresting all the members of the fruit growers' coordination committee — that gave the first call for the 'March to Muzaffarabad' — from the Sopore fruit mandi had had no effect. Many fruit growers managed to evade protest and joined the march.

While police also seized many trucks on Sunday night to prevent growers from taking their produce to Pakistan Occupied Kashmir, as threatened, growers had managed to arrange dozens of vehicles, including trucks, trolleys and pick-up vans.

"We gave enough time to the Government to open the National Highway, but they did nothing," said Ghulam Mohammad Malik, General Secretary, Sopore Fruit Growers' Association. "The sea of people who are marching towards the LoC is a testimony that nobody can prevent us from sending our fruit towards Muzuffarabad."

Even children of fruit growers joined the march. "Our fruit is being looted and trucks attacked at Jammu, Kathua and Punjab. So the march is our last option," said Abid Bashir, 13, who was part of the protest and had come from Rohema Rafiabad, Jammu and Kashmir's apple bowl. "My father has no income other than what he earns from fruit."

Heading: For first time, IAF joins multi-nation air exercise in US - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress today termed the all-party delegation's visit to Jammu and Srinagar as "successful" and castigated the BJP for questioning the existence of an economic blockade on the Jammu-Srinagar highway.

"This is a matter of regret that BJP representative (Arun Jaitley) did not even wait for the delegation to meet and apprise the Prime Minister... The remarks they gave today are irresponsible. To say that there is no economic blockade is far from the truth... The BJP is giving priority to its political interest over national interest," AICC spokesperson Manish Tewari told reporters.

The Congress leadership, meanwhile, is perturbed about a section of the leaders choosing to go public with their views, contrary to those of the party. Senior party leader Dr Karan Singh and Udhampur MP Chaudhury Lal Singh have demanded the removal of Governor N N Vohra. Lal Singh along with the Jammu MP and party MLAs have been open about their sympathy with the agitators in Jammu, terming it a "spontaneous" outburst of Jammu people who were discriminated against in the past 60 years.

The Congress today sought to play these remarks down saying that they could be airing "personal opinion" and no party MLA or MP was involved in the agitation. "If any instance of anybody being involved in the agitation in any capacity is found, the party will take action (against them)," Tewari said.

Heading: SC: no immunity to Speaker’s staff - Indian Express
Content:
India marked it first-ever presence in the prestigious Red Flag exercise at the Nellis Airbase in Nevada on Sunday. The IAF contingent has been in the US for several weeks but the formal inauguration of the exercise took place on Sunday after a detailed mission planning by the participating countries.

IAF, which is participating with eight Su-30s, two IL-78 tankers and an IL-76 aircraft will engage the French Air Force (with Rafale fighters), South Korean Air Force (with F-15s) and the US Air Force with their F-15s and F-16s.

A combined force of IAF, the visiting Air Forces and a large USAF element would be part of the Blue Forces (friendly) which would engage in combat with the Red Forces that would consist of the "Aggressors" with F-15s & F-16s aircraft of the USAF.

"The replication of the air war would see the IAF's Su-30 aircraft participating in suppression of enemy air defence (SEAD) air-to-air and air-to-ground missions. The IL-78 tankers and USAF AWACS would be in active support role. The IL-76 would undertake tactical transport operations & large force engagements operations," IAF spokesperson Wing Commander Mahesh Upasani, who is part of the Indian delegation in Nellis, said.

The entire exercise would be monitored in real time on screens on ground and the war game would be made realistic by 'kill removal' — removal of the pilots and aircraft assumed shot by the enemy.

Heading: SC to hear plea for moratorium on GM crop today - Indian Express
Content:
Agreeing to examine a petition filed by the Madhya Pradesh Lokayukta against the Assembly Speaker, the Supreme Court on Monday clarified that though a Speaker enjoys immunity, it is not granted to any official working under him in his office.

The privilege enjoyed by the Speaker would not be available even to the Secretary of Vidhan Sabha, noted a Bench comprising Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justice J M Panchal.

"All the actions attributed to the Speaker enjoy immunity. But how can other employees enjoy immunity?" the Bench asked senior counsel Mukul Rohtagi, appearing for the Madhya Pradesh Speaker.

The court refused to accept the submission that since the Speaker was in charge of the House, a notice by the Lokayukta to the officials under him amounted to breach of privilege.

"Secretary has no privilege. It is only the legislators who enjoy the immunity," the Bench observed, adding it appeared that some of the legislators wanted to protect "rightly or wrongly" the officials served with notice by the ombudsman.

Senior counsel Harish Salve on behalf of the Lokayukta argued that the Speaker's action "was a brazen attempt to protect some officials and his action was a serious issue".

He submitted that the Speaker had acted without jurisdiction and had "no such sweeping power" to act in the name of breach of privilege.

In November 2007, the apex court had stayed a notice issued by the MP Speaker to Lokayukta Justice (retd) Ripusudan Dayal "for breach of privilege".

The Speaker had issued the notice against the Lokayukta and others in his office after the ombudsman initiated an inquiry against officials of the State Legislative Department for irregularities involving public funds amounting to Rs 2 crore in connection with the laying of a road connecting the Assembly building.

While issuing a notice to the Speaker, the apex court had also sought a para-wise reply from the ombudsman on the issue.

Heading: Army performs another multiple-organ transplant - Indian Express
Content:
An application seeking a complete moratorium on release of any genetically-modified (GM) crops in the environment till an independent testing facility is set up in India, will be listed for hearing in the Supreme Court on Tuesday.

A "review of six years of Bt cotton experience" is sought on the opinion of Dr P M Bhargava, the noted microbiological expert. He says "it is necessary that review must take place during a full moratorium on all GM crops, including Bt cotton" — a view that will be placed before a Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan.

Highlighting several lacunas in the present bio-testing system, Aruna Rodrigues, who had earlier filed a PIL, has now moved an application urging the court to issue directions to the Union Government for imposing a ban on import of any GM product.

She has pointed to the extensive communication between Dr P M Bhargava, an international expert in molecular biology, and Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (GEAC). GEAC is the sole authority to approve the release of genetically-modified organisms (GMOs) under the 1989 Rules.

Following the apex court directions on February 13, 2008, Dr Bhargava, the founder director of Centre for Cell and Molecular Biology, Hyderabad, and Dr Swaminathan of Swaminathan Research Foundation, Chennai, were invited to meetings "whenever any application for seeking approval for release of GMO is taken up".

The applicant claims what transpired in the meetings, as also known through the communication between the GEAC and Dr Bhargava, is "a very alarming picture of the manner in which clearances have been given for environmental release of GMOs".

Advocate Prashant Bhushan, counsel for Rodrigues, says a vast majority of bio-safety tests, which are required before such crops are allowed for safe release into the environment, are not being conducted. Whatever tests are being done are being carried out by the applicant company, "which has a clear commercial interest".

The application has also underlined the need for having an independent testing laboratory with adequate technical capacity.

Heading: Tigers migrating from Rajaji’s western section - Indian Express
Content:
The Army has performed another complicated multiple-organ transplant with an officer's 67-year-old mother giving new life to five soldiers across the country.

Lt Col Dinesh Talwar, posted along the LoC, consented to donate the organs of his mother, Usha Tanwar, who was declared brain dead by doctors at the Army Hospital (R&R) on Saturday.

The liver was transplanted into a 24-year-old soldier suffering from cirrhosis of liver, one kidney was transplanted into a 54-year-old veteran suffering from an end-stage kidney disease while the second kidney was flown to Command Hospital, Pune, for transplantation to another veteran.

Lt Gen OP Mathew, commandant of Army Hospital (R&R), said that this was the tenth multi-organ donation at the hospital. "The heart valves have been stored for later use. The eyes will be used on Monday for two different individuals who have lost their total vision in one eye," an Army spokesperson said.

The operation was performed by the Armed Forces Organ Retrieval and Transplantation Authority (AORTA), established last year to increase awareness on brain death and promote organ donation. Over 2,000 serving personnel, veterans and their families have pledged to donate their organs.

Heading: Bangalore protests as fresh curbs derail nightlife - Indian Express
Content:
The western section of Rajaji National park has seen a decline in its tiger population over the last three years. According to officials, the number of tigers in this section has come down to as low as one or two from six or seven.

Playing down the possibility of poaching, Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forests Shrikant Chandola says that this could be because of tigers having migrated from this section of the forest because of the human colonies close by. He added that the park has more than a dozen tigers, mostly concentrated in the eastern section of the national park.

Talking to media persons on the eve of the 25th anniversary of the Rajaji National Park, Chandola also gave an account of the elephant population in the forest. He disclosed that in the last four years, four elephants have died on account of coming in contact with electric fences put by farmers to save their farms from the animals. "Steps are being taken to prevent this man-animal conflict. A major step in this direction is the decentralization of the compensation disbursement process to the farmers," he said.

On the positive side, there have been no elephant deaths due to collisions with the trains since 2002.

"This has been possible on account of joint efforts of the forest department and the Indian railways. Joint patrolling along the tracks that run through the park has been very helpful in checking accidents. There have been occasions when railway drivers have reduced their speed or even stopped trains on coming to know of elephants in the vicinity of the tracks," Chandola disclosed.

During the period between 1987 and 2002, a total of 21 elephants had lost their lives after colliding with the trains on this stretch.

Another good news on the elephant front is that the sex ratio amongst elephants in the Park is very good. It stands at 2.5 females for every male tusker. Authorities point out that in the south, this ratio is as bad as 100 females for every tusker. This has been on account of large scale poaching of tuskers for ivory by forest brigands.

Chandola also disclosed that the final notification on the creation of Rajaji National Park is expected to come very soon.

The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests Dr R B S Rawat said that as a part of the silver jubilee celebrations of the park, special emphasis will be laid on the ecological development of the area with the help of the people living on the fringes. He said that special efforts will be made to generate awareness on wildlife conservation amongst the school children living in these fringe villages.

Heading: Terror politics: Cong wants probe into Surat bombs - Indian Express
Content:
Exactly three years ago when the then Dharam Singh-led Congress-JDS government did it, it was called the 'Talibanisation of Bangalore'. Now with the new BJP Government tightening the screws on nightlife in Bangalore, protestors are calling it 'Bangalore bleeding'.

With the Bangalore police deciding to go strictly by the book again all restaurants with live bands and dancing have been banned. Over the past two Sundays musicians, artistes, disc jockeys and Bangalore's partying public have been protesting the reinforced ban at the Mahatma Gandhi statue in central Bangalore. Participating in this Sunday's protests, writer and theatre personality Girish Karnad said the decision to ban live music lacked logic. "It will affect artistes adversely. Instead of going after criminals the police are going after musicians," he said.

Despite the protests featuring over 1000 people on Sunday, the Bangalore police cracked down on as many as 32 discotheques operating without valid licenses in the city. Nightlife in the city is governed by 'The licensing and controlling of places of public entertainment (Bangalore City) order, 2005' and the Karnataka Excise Act of 1965.

The licensing order makes it mandatory for all places offering live entertainment to be licensed by the police after meeting strict standards. The Act prevents places serving alcohol from staying open beyond 11:30 pm and women from dancing in places where alcohol is sold.

Though, the state home department has indicated a move to modify the laws to reduce restrictions on nightlife, no legislative action has been taken yet. New Bangalore police commissioner Shankar Bidari has stated that he is willing to consider relaxation of nightlife rules if he receives sufficient representation from the public.

The existing laws has resulted in a tussle between owners of lower end dance bars and the upper end lounge bars and discotheques. The introduction of the licensing rules for cabarets, dance bars, discotheques and live bands in June 2005 had resulted in a clampdown on all forms of dancing at public entertainment spots in Bangalore.

However, in December 2005, following appeals by owners of establishments, the Supreme Court permitted live bands and dancing in restaurants and hotels on the condition that the establishments didn't encourage prostitution or indecent shows. While the Bangalore police allowed dancing and live music shows at pubs, restaurants, nightclubs and discotheques, they imposed a more stringent curb on dance bars on the grounds that they encouraged prostitution. This discrimination has been challenged by owners of dance bars in the High Court resulting in a complete clampdown on all nightlife.

Heading: Another ceasefire violation on LoC, India retaliates - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress on Monday demanded a CBI investigation into the planting of bombs in Surat, saying if the Gujarat Government is clear on the issue, it should hand over the probe to the premier investigating agency.

Reacting to the statement of Puri Shankaracharya Adhokshanand Devteerth in Guwahati where he alleged that the discovery of live bombs in Surat was a conspiracy of Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi, Congress spokesman Manish Tewari said the state Government should come clear on it.

Tewari claimed the Congress was not making an allegation but said the Shankacharya's allegations were serious.

The party spokesman said senior Congress leader Digvijay Singh has already indicated about it in Uttar Pradesh on Sunday. Singh had said that people should take cognisance of the fact that bomb blasts took place in the country when the BJP was in trouble.

"Whenever BJP is in trouble, bomb blasts take place in the country ...," Singh had said while addressing a two-day party convention of the Congress' state unit.

Heading: Defence PRO passes away - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another violation of the 2003 ceasefire agreement, Pakistani Army troops lobbed 60 mm mortars and directed small arms fire at Indian posts in the Poonch sector on Monday afternoon. While no casualties were reported on the Indian side, the Army retaliated and targeted the Pakistani post with small arms fire.

A senior Army officer said that Pakistani troops attacked the Indian post at 12.30 in the afternoon. Officers said there was no indication that the firing was carried out to divert attention from infiltrators attempting to cross the fence in the area.

Monday's incident is the 22nd time that Pakistan has violated the ceasefire agreement this year. The incidents come after a relatively quiete four years where the ceasefire agreement was upheld by both sides.

In the last incident that took place a week ago in the Nowgam Sector, a BSF posts was taregeted by small arms fire. On July 28, a group of Pakistani soldiers crossed the LoC in the same sector and shot dead an Indian Jawan after objecting to an observation post on the border. Four Pakistani soldiers were also killed in the incident.

Heading: Donning the messiahs role - Indian Express
Content: The Public Relations Officer (PRO) of the Ministry of Defence (Palam Area and Western Air Command), Wing Commander Manish Gandhi, passed away on Sunday after a long battle with cancer. His mortal remains were consigned to flames with full military honours at the Brar Square Crematorium on Monday. Senior officials of the Directorate of Public Relations, Ministry of Defence, the Western Air Command, the Indian Air Force, a number of journalists, friends and relations paid their last respects to the officer before the funeral. Born on July 16, 1966, Wg Cdr Gandhi was commissioned in the Administrative Branch of the Indian Air Force on December 17 1988. He leaves behind his wife, son and daughter.

Heading: Abhinav India Bindra - Indian Express
Content:
Telugu megastar Chiranjeevi inaugurated his state-of-the-art party office at 12:50 am on Monday at Banjara Hills Road No 45. The party office is close to his brother-in-law Allu Arvind's film company, Geeta Arts. The megastar performed pooja with his entire family and a few friends. The actor is expected to launch his party on August 15 or on August 22, his birthday. By entering politics, Chiranjeevi, 53, joins yesteryears matinee idol, N T Rama Rao.

His three-storey and centrally-airconditioned party office has become the talk of the town with tastefully done interiors, hi-end facilities and a press conference room. The megastar has reserved for himself a modest cabin. The office is fully computertised with wi-fi and can be easily mistaken for a software company. At least a dozen close circuit TV cameras have been installed in the office.

Though it was drizzling, Chiranjeevi chose the hour after midnight, as it was an auspicious time according to the Telugu calendar. A calm and composed actor told reporters what he has been repeating over the past few months and ended the brief interaction with the media by making a politically correct statement.

"I know my fans are waiting for me to announce my party. I will not disappoint them. They have to just wait for a few more days.
